findings.title: B2's REPA alignment reads the DiT at sigma=0.0089 (the finished image), so the transfer channel is nearly degenerate
findings.detail: student_rollout keeps grad and arms the hook only on the LAST step (rank_utils.py:70-79). With the run's scheduler the 4-step rollout sigmas are [1.0, 0.8577, 0.6022, 0.0089, 0.0] (log line '[rank] negatives ... rollout sigmas'), so the hooked forward's input is z at sigma=0.0089 (timestep 8.9): essentially the final image. The alignment target is sg[g(P(z_K))] with z_K = z_3 - 0.0089*v (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1393-1396, 1421), i.e. a near-deterministic function of that same input, so the loss can be driven down by the 2048-wide projector alone without changing generation. That step's velocity is multiplied by delta-sigma=-0.0089, so it barely affects samples, and the consistency branch never feeds the student at that noise level (student inputs are k-delta in 1..6, sigma 0.338..0.948; K=8 sigmas [1.0,0.9475,0.8828,0.8008,0.6938,0.548,0.338,0.0089]). REPA's mechanism relies on aligning features of NOISY inputs to a target the input does not already contain; here neither holds.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:70-79; phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1393-1394,1419-1431; scheduler check: 4-step sigmas [1.0,0.8577,0.6022,0.0089,0.0], K=8 student-input sigma range 0.338..0.948; logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151399.out: align loss 0.98 at step 0 -> 0.078 at step 300 (fits in <300 updates, consistent with a trivially fittable target); align-probe ||grad align|| 1.2-1.6 at step 0 (non-zero, so the path is live but weak).
findings.consequence: A B2 null cannot be read as 'representation transfer does not help'; it tests the weakest possible version of the design note's Variant B. A B2 positive would need another explanation.
findings.fix: Add a --align_step k (or random k per caption) and keep grad through THAT forward only (same cost as now: one grad-enabled forward); hook the step whose input is sigma 0.6022 or 0.8577. Optionally also hook the consistency forward's supervised states (sigma 0.34-0.95) with target sg[g(P(z_K))] of the caption's own rollout; consider per-token cosine (REPA) instead of mean-pooled.

findings.title: B1/A confound: the head's Jacobian gain makes the shaped reward 2-3x stronger than 'ours' by step 1000, so B1-vs-ours mixes 'prompt-aware direction' with 'reward strength'
findings.detail: The reward in B1/A is -80*<g(P(x_hat)), g(u_ref)> (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1253-1256); its gradient w.r.t. the student scales with J_g. Nothing renormalises it, and with grad_clip=1 always active (pre-clip 120-180) only the SHARE of each term in the update direction matters. Saved B1 s0 heads on the replay DINO embeddings: cos(g(e),e) 0.944 (step 500) -> 0.881 (1000) -> 0.850 (1500) -> 0.804 (2000), |W_fc2| 2.8 -> 6.5, and the ratio ||d<g(e),g(u)>/de|| / ||d<e,u>/de|| = 0.88 -> 1.16 -> 1.38 -> 1.55; A s0 at 1000: cos 0.72, gain 1.49. In the live probes ||grad reward|| goes 90-110 (step 0) -> 30-62 (500) -> 146-215 (1000) while ||grad CD|| stays 190-360, i.e. reward/CD share 0.25-0.33 -> 0.60-0.97 (B1 s0) and 0.76 (A s0). The control 'ours' runs have reward_grad_probe_every=0 (args.json), so its own share is unmeasured (the projector refresh could also move it). The same head drift lowers the mean shaped cosine (0.489 raw -> 0.435 shaped at step 2000), which is what 'reward/r_mean drifts down' in REVIEW_CONTEXT shows; reward/r_mean is a different quantity in B1/A vs B2/ours.
findings.evidence: train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1253-1259; logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151302.out [reward-probe] step 0/500/1000 lines; logs/...-151316.out step 1000 ratio 0.7648; head analysis on checkpoints/phaseW/phaseW_CD_dinop_hard_3k-rewRi-s16-rankB1-hp1-acc4_s0_151302/rank_head_step{500,1000,1500,2000}.pt; checkpoints/phaseW/phaseW_CD_dinop_hard_3k-rewRi-s16-hp1-acc4_s0_145176/args.json reward_grad_probe_every=0.
findings.consequence: Any B1/A gain over ours could be a larger effective reward weight, and any loss could be reward over-driving (the 118k audit already showed reward share matters). The contrast does not isolate the head's prompt-awareness.
findings.fix: (a) Measure it: at probe steps also compute the raw reward's gradient norm on the same x_hat (one extra autograd.grad) and log shaped/raw; enable --reward_grad_probe_every 500 on the control runs. (b) Control it: normalise the shaped reward gradient (divide _r by sg[||J_g^T g(u)||] estimated per step, or scale lambda by the running shaped/raw ratio), or add a 'ours + lambda_reward matched to the measured share' arm. (c) Decisive control at equal head dynamics: shuffled negatives (negatives drawn from another caption) so g moves and gains without prompt information; kappa->inf is the cheaper but weaker version.

findings.title: probe_params (i % 4 == 0) never probes any attention/adaLN weight matrix, so the lambda_rank=1.3 / lambda_align=60 '20 percent' calibration is measured on biases and norm scales only
findings.detail: Every non-dual JointTransformerBlock has 32 parameter tensors and dual blocks 42, so the fixed stride selects the same roles in every block. From checkpoint_step500's key order the 228-tensor subset consists of 26 roles dominated by ff.net.0.proj.bias, ff_context.net.0.proj.bias, norm1.linear.bias, attn.norm_k.weight, to_k.bias, add_k_proj.bias, add_q_proj.bias, to_add_out.bias (16-17 blocks each); 21 of 42 block roles are never probed, including norm1.linear.weight, to_q/to_k/to_v/to_out.0/to_add_out.weight and add_{q,k,v}_proj.weight. Rank/align vs CD ratios on biases need not equal the ratios on the weight matrices that carry most of the gradient norm and most of the update. Also note the probe is per single caption (||grad CD|| 200-500 on the subset) while the accumulated 16-caption pre-clip norm is 120-180, so the per-caption gradient is mostly noise and the '20 percent share' is not the share in the mean update.
findings.evidence: phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:668-671, 1261-1263, 1409-1411, 1424-1426; key analysis of checkpoints/phaseW/phaseW_CD_dinop_hard_3k-rewRi-s16-rankB1-hp1-acc4_s0_151302/checkpoint_step500.pt (909 tensors; blocks 42/42/42/.../32/32/26); phaseW/launch_rank.sh comment 'Weights from the smoke'.
findings.consequence: lambda_rank and lambda_align may be far from the intended 20 percent share on the parameters that matter; the arms could be under- or over-driven, which changes what a null means.
findings.fix: Use a stratified fixed subset (e.g. every 4th tensor with an offset that includes weights, or a seeded random 25 percent of tensors), or compute the two full norms sequentially (one autograd.grad at a time, freeing between) at probe steps; report the share on the accumulated update once per 500 steps as well.

findings.title: Held-out probe leaks the projector's training captions: 61 of its 300 captions are in P's 22k train split (70 in P's 27k shards); the replay set is not excluded either
findings.detail: probe_heldout.py excludes only the 3k pool (--exclude default phaseN/coco_selection_dinopatch; line 74-77 filters by prompt and reference of that pool). The projector P was pretrained on phaseW/latent_scorer/shards (27,000 idx, 22,000 'train'). Intersecting the probe's record idx with the shards: 61 in train, 9 in val/test, 70 total of 300. The 'latent' and 'latent_g' spaces are therefore not held-out for P (its cosine and ranking-KL losses saw those captions' teacher candidates and u_ref). replay_2k.pt carries no idx so its overlap cannot be tested; it is presumably drawn from the same shards.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/probe_heldout.py:60,74-77; phaseW/rank/probe/base.json records; phaseW/latent_scorer/shards/shard*.pt idx/split (10 files, 14G); phaseW/latent_scorer/train_projector.py:103-105.
findings.consequence: The latent-space probe numbers (base 0.499, naive 0.538, ours 0.537) and any future latent_g numbers for trained heads are partly in-sample for P; rgb/rgb_g are unaffected (frozen DINO).
findings.fix: Exclude idx with split=='train' (and val/test if P's early stopping used them) from `held`, and exclude the replay set by regenerating replay_2k with an idx field; report latent-space accuracies on the remaining ~230 captions, or add the 'seen by P' flag per record and report both strata.

findings.title: B1 applies a head fitted on P(z_K) of sharp 4-step rollouts to P(x_hat) of blurry one-step Tweedie estimates at sigma 0.34-0.55; nothing monitors the ranking in that space
findings.detail: The head is trained only on _e = P(z_K) (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1396-1402) but the reward that reaches the student uses P(x_hat) of the two least-noisy supervised inputs (1245-1256), whose inputs are at sigma 0.338-0.548 (stu_idx 5-6 of the K=8 grid); x_hat is a one-step clean estimate, which the project's own diagnostics put 17-27 percent off the endpoint. The head's shaping learned on the rollout distribution may not carry over to x_hat, and there is no in-training measure of pairwise accuracy or margin in the x_hat space (rank/acc_* are all on z_K).
findings.consequence: A B1 null could be a transfer failure between the two input distributions rather than a failure of prompt-aware shaping; a positive is harder to attribute.
findings.fix: Cheap monitor: at probe steps compute for the positive caption the shaped and raw cosine of P(x_hat) vs u_ref and P(z_K) vs u_ref and log their correlation; better: also train the head on the positive's P(x_hat) paired with negatives' P(x_hat) at the same state (requires rolling the negatives on the teacher grid, ~3x rollout cost, or reusing the student's rollout states z_k at sigma 0.6 with a one-step Tweedie).

findings.title: README claim 'captions without negatives contribute no loss' is false for B2 (alignment on 100 percent of captions) and A wastes grad rollouts on the 39 percent without negatives
findings.detail: The alignment term (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1419-1432) is computed for every caption, including the 1,184 without negatives, so B2's transfer channel runs on all captions while the head only learns on 61 percent. In A, _grad_all rollouts run with full 4-step gradient even when _l_rank = _Rs.sum()*0.0 (1390-1394, 1407), which is why A costs 8.3 s/update vs 4.0 for B1. DDP parity is why it is done unconditionally, but the cost could be avoided by sorting captions so every rank sees the same negatives-present flag per micro-step, or by gathering the flag with one all_reduce before the rollout.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/README.md:19-23; phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1384-1394,1405-1407,1419-1432; [rank] log negs/caption 1.2-1.5 (3884/3000=1.29).
findings.consequence: Documentation/interpretation only for B2 (the align term is a general REPA regulariser on every caption, not a ranking-specific one); ~2x wasted compute in A.
findings.fix: Fix the README sentence; for A, all_reduce a 'has negatives' flag (or a per-update sort) and run no-grad rollouts when no rank needs gradient.

findings.title: rank_utils.py is untracked, so it is in neither the run's git_diff.patch nor the wandb source artifact; provenance of the ranking code depends on nobody editing it

findings.title: rank/loss is dominated by log(1+m) and acc_shaped is in-sample and caption-weighted; the RGB monitor (8 captions) is noise
findings.detail: ranking_loss = logsumexp(R/kappa) - R_pos/kappa has chance level log(1+m) (0.69/1.10/1.39 for m=1/2/3), so the logged window mean moves with negatives-per-window (B1: 1.05 -> 1.09 -> 1.12 over steps 50-150 while acc rises 0.548 -> 0.560). pairwise_acc averages per caption (a 1-negative caption weighs as much as a 3-negative one), on the head's own training rollouts. acc_rgb uses the last 8 captions (about 10 pairs): B1 and A log identical 0.875 at steps 100 and 150, and B1 swings 0.875 -> 0.50 by 2100.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:85-94; phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1433-1441,1465-1477; logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151302.out and -151316.out [rank] lines.
findings.consequence: Training-time ranking metrics overstate progress and are not comparable across windows/arms; the RGB monitor cannot detect anything.
findings.fix: Log loss - log(1+m) (or the per-caption softmax probability of the positive), pair-weighted accuracy, and run the RGB check on >=64 buffered rollouts every 500 steps (decode is ~60 ms/image).

findings.title: Head and align projector run at constant lr 1e-4 while the student's lr decays to 0; the saved final head is not the one the student last adapted to
findings.detail: rank_head_opt and align_opt have no schedule (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:890,897) whereas the student is cosine-to-0. Late in training the reward space keeps moving at full speed while the student cannot follow; harmless for the student's weights but the final head (used by the held-out probe's latent_g/rgb_g) diverges from the head that shaped the student, and the step-2000/2500/final weight average is evaluated against one head.
findings.evidence: phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:890,897,1457-1464; head drift cos(g(e),e) 0.94->0.80 across 500-2000 in B1 s0.
findings.consequence: Probe numbers 'through the trained head' conflate the head's continued drift with the student's state.
findings.fix: Tie the head/align lr to the student's schedule (a LambdaLR with the same _lr_mult), and probe with the head saved at the same step as the checkpoint being evaluated.

findings.title: Controls and monitors that would make the test decisive at low cost
findings.detail: (1) Shuffled-negatives control for B1 (negatives borrowed from another caption; same head dynamics and gain, no prompt information): one flag, no extra compute; it is the direct answer to F2. (2) kappa->inf (or --rank_head_lr 0) arm: recovers ours exactly by construction and doubles as a bit-level regression test of RNG isolation. (3) Log at probe steps the raw and shaped reward gradient norms on the same x_hat and the cosine between them (two autograd.grad calls, already budgeted). (4) Enable --reward_grad_probe_every 500 on the naive/ours controls so the reward share is known in the reference. (5) For B2, --align_step with a mid-trajectory step (F1). (6) Train the head on true-DINO features of decoded rollouts as well (the RGB monitor already decodes them): removes the P-vs-DINO gap from the head's target and lets rgb_g be a fair probe. (7) In the probe, report pair-weighted accuracy, AUC of margins and per-family counts with binomial CIs; 833 pairs give about +-0.034 at 95 percent, so per-family differences of 0.05-0.1 are not resolvable.
findings.evidence: phaseW/launch_rank.sh EXTRA table; train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1260-1270 (probe scaffolding exists); phaseW/rank/probe_heldout.py:139-150.
findings.consequence: Without (1)/(3)/(4) a B1/A result cannot be attributed to prompt-awareness rather than reward strength; without (5) B2 is a weak test.
findings.fix: Add flags --rank_shuffle_negs, --align_step, and the probe logging; launch the shuffled-negatives B1 arm with the next seed batch.

validated: Gradient paths match the claims: the head g trains only from _l_head on _e.detach() (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1400-1402); the shaped reward (1256), A's ranking term (1406) and B2's target (1421) all use head_apply(..., False) = torch.func.functional_call with detached parameters (rank_utils.py:39-45), so the student never trains g and g never sees the student's gradient; align.proj is trained only through _l_align inside loss (1431) and its own optimizer (1462-1464); RankHead has no buffers, so functional_call is complete.

Identity at init and 'lambda_rank = 0 recovers ours': fc2 is zero-initialised (rank_utils.py:32-33), LatentProjector.forward returns F.normalize(...) (phaseW/latent_scorer/train_projector.py:50) and ref_emb_3k.pt entries are unit vectors (norms 1.0000 checked), so g(e)=e at step 0 and the shaped reward equals the raw reward exactly.

ranking_loss is the correct partial-order softmax cross-entropy (logsumexp(R/kappa) - R[0]/kappa, rank_utils.py:85-88); pairwise_acc is the fraction of negatives the positive outranks; margin = R_pos - mean(R_neg).

Rollout schedule: rollout_schedule reads the 4-step sigmas/timesteps and restores K=8 (rank_utils.py:48-55); the consistency branch calls rollout_states, which re-sets K every micro-step before pipe.scheduler.timesteps is read (trainer:59-61, 1024, 1075), so no scheduler state leaks. The rollout sigmas [1.0,0.8577,0.6022,0.0089,0.0] are exactly the eval sampler's: exp0/phaseA_generate.py uses euler_cfg_sample (exp0/generate_candidates.py:74-99) with the same scheduler, fp32 step then bf16 cast, and one conditional pass at cfg 1; student_rollout (rank_utils.py:67-82) has the same update. Only difference: eval casts the transformer weights to bf16, training runs fp32 weights under bf16 autocast.

grad / grad_last handling: steps run under no_grad except the requested ones; the bf16 cast between steps is differentiable so A's chain is intact; the hook is armed only on the last step and disarmed before any backward, so the checkpoint recomputation (which re-fires the forward hook) cannot overwrite _h.

AlignHook with non-reentrant checkpointing: diffusers 0.32.2 uses torch.utils.checkpoint with use_reentrant=False (transformer_sd3.py:416), JointTransformerBlock returns (encoder_hidden_states, hidden_states) (attention.py:257) so out[-1] is the image-token stream; the captured tensor has a grad_fn (the guard in features() would raise otherwise) and the live [align-probe] lines show finite ||grad align|| 1.2-1.6 on student parameters, so the path into blocks 1-8 is real; in_dim = 24*64 = 1536 matches.

DDP parity: the rank block condition (1379) is rank-agnostic and rollouts run on every rank every micro-step, including m=1 rollouts for captions without negatives; _l_head.backward() touches no DDP-managed parameter; the rank-0-only probes use torch.autograd.grad (no AccumulateGrad hooks, no collectives); all_reduce_grads for head/align is reached by every rank at the same point after opt.step(); no_grad DDP forwards only toggle the buffer-sync flag (pos_embed is a constant non-persistent buffer). Empirically the 4-GPU smoke passed (phaseW/rank/smoke/results.txt rc=0 for B1/B2/A) and the live runs passed 2200 (B1 s0), 1050 (A s0) and 800 (B2 s1) updates without hangs or 'marked ready twice' errors.

Head/align optimizers: (_l_head/accum).backward() accumulates over the accum micro-steps, grads are all-reduced (mean over world), clipped at 1.0, stepped once per update and zeroed with set_to_none after the step (1457-1464); align.proj receives grads through loss/accum; neither is inside the student's optimizer or the student's clip (clip_grad_norm_(student_module.parameters()) at 1454); the 2x8 and 4x4 placements give the same effective batch of 16 for the student, the head and the projector.

Shaped reward: computed on the two least-noisy supervised inputs (reward_states=2, 1245-1246) as <g(P(x_hat)), g(u_ref)> with detached head weights (1256), added as -80*mean (1259, 1272); B2's args.json has rank_shaped_reward=False and rank_lambda=0, B1's has shaped=True/align 0, A's has backprop/1.3/shaped=True, all matching README and launch_rank.sh.

RNG isolation: rollout_noise uses a private generator keyed by (seed, rank, micro) (rank_utils.py:163-166; no cross-rank or cross-seed collisions for rank<4); head and align init run under manual_seed with CPU and CUDA RNG states saved and restored (trainer:884-898); the rollouts, encode_prompt and the monitors draw no global randomness. Empirical confirmation: the step-0 [reward-probe] values are identical across B1 s0, A s0 and B2 s0 (cd=49.4596, r=0.2724) and B1 vs A share the same four captions per update through step 500 (cd 52.27/58.00/31.04/48.34 vs 52.51/59.31/31.18/48.09).

Negatives pairing: negatives_3k.json is keyed by the selection cache's idx and all 1,816 source prompts equal the cache prompt for that idx (0 mismatches); 3,884 negatives with the stated 929/210/677 histogram; ref_emb_3k.pt is a dict idx -> unit 768-vector over the 3,000 pool idx; rank_negs[:rank_m] truncation is a no-op (<=3 stored).

RGB monitor and rank_buf: main-rank only, keeps the last 16 (uses 8) rollouts of captions with negatives, decodes them and ranks with the true DINO scorer raw and through g under no_grad; it never touches training state.
Head saving: rank_head_step*.pt / rank_head_final.pt store head + align_proj + rank_args (1665-1668, 1679-1682); probe_heldout.py rebuilds RankHead(768) with the default width 1024 = training width.

Logging windows: rank_stats are printed/logged at gstep % log_every == 0 before the reset at 1640-1645; acc_rgb/acc_rgb_shaped/g_rank/g_align are 'last reading' values by design; train/loss_cd is CD-only (captured at 1271 before the reward is added), so the cross-arm consistency-loss comparison in REVIEW_CONTEXT is valid even though train/loss includes the rank/align/reward terms.

Smoke calibration reproduces: at weight 1 the rank/CD ratios are 0.068-0.35 and align/CD 0.0019-0.005 (phaseW/rank/smoke/{A,B2}.log), matching the README's numbers; lambda 1.3/60 give 0.09-0.46 and 0.13-0.31 at step 0 in the live runs (subject to F3).

Code provenance: the trainer diff embedded in all five run dirs is md5-identical to the current working-tree diff, and rank_utils.py / the trainer were last modified at 02:35 / 02:57 on 2026-09-16, before every job start (03:05 onward), so the reviewed code is the code that ran.

2 GPUs x accum 8 vs 4 x 4 differs only in seed-like ways (DistributedSampler shard assignment, rollout_noise keyed by (rank, micro), rank 0's rbuf/rank_buf recency); n_visits only feeds target_schedule arms, which these are not; effective batch, LR schedule and head/projector batch are identical.
lenses.summary: Trainer correctness of the ranking additions is sound: every gradient path does what REVIEW_CONTEXT claims (head trains only on detached rollouts; the student sees the ranking only in A and only through detached head weights; B2's alignment target is stopped; the shaped reward trains the student only), the rollout is the eval sampler's schedule and update, scheduler state is restored, RNG isolation holds (identical step-0 losses across arms and shared caption order B1 vs A through step 500), DDP parity holds by construction and empirically, the head/align optimizers accumulate and all-reduce correctly, and the arms' args.json match the launcher and README. The code that ran is the working tree. The problems are design-level, not bugs. Two are serious: (F1) B2 hooks the DiT at sigma=0.0089, where the input is the finished image and the target is a near-function of that input, so the REPA channel is close to degenerate and its fast-falling align loss (1.0 -> 0.08 in <300 updates) is expected; (F2) in B1/A the head's Jacobian gain (measured 0.88x -> 1.55x on saved heads; live reward/CD gradient share 0.25-0.33 -> 0.6-0.97 by step 1000) makes the shaped reward 2-3x stronger than 'ours' under always-active clipping, so B1-vs-ours confounds prompt-aware direction with reward strength, and the control has no probes to compare against. Medium items: the gradient probe subset never includes any weight matrix (lambda calibration on biases/norms), the held-out probe leaks 61-70 of 300 captions from the projector's pretraining, and the head is fitted on P(z_K) of rollouts but applied to P(x_hat) at sigma 0.34-0.55 with no monitor in that space. Cheapest decisive additions: a shuffled-negatives B1 arm, reward probes on the controls plus a raw-vs-shaped gradient log, and an --align_step at a mid-trajectory sigma for B2.

findings.title: B2 aligns the DiT at sigma=0.009 (the last rollout step): an autoencoding regression, not REPA transfer
findings.detail: student_rollout keeps grad only through the LAST forward (grad_last) and AlignHook captures block 8 there. The 4-step schedule the trainer logs is [1.0, 0.858, 0.602, 0.009, 0.0] (diffusers' double-shifted sigma_min), so the aligned forward takes z_3 at sigma=0.009, i.e. an essentially clean latent, and its target g(P(z_K)) with z_K = z_3 + 0.009*v is a function of (almost) the same tensor. The term therefore teaches blocks 1-8 to predict the shaped embedding of their own nearly-clean input. The note's L_align aligns h_theta(x_t) at noisy states to the clean image's projected features so that the geometry reaches the steps that decide composition (sigma 1 -> 0.6); none of those steps receives any alignment gradient here.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:69-81 (ctx grad only when `last`), phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1393-1394,1419-1431; logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151399.out '[rank] negatives ... rollout sigmas [1.0, 0.858, 0.602, 0.009, 0.0]'; align loss 0.98 -> 0.0763 by step 350 (151399), 0.06-0.20 at 500 (151328/151336) and ratio at lambda 60 0.12-0.70 of the CD gradient.
findings.consequence: B2 as run cannot transfer prompt-awareness into generation; a B2 null (or effect) says nothing about the note's Variant B, and the 'B de-risks A' logic is void.
findings.fix: Capture at the FIRST rollout step (input = the shared noise, so block-8 tokens differ only through the prompt: a genuinely prompt-conditioned prediction of the shaped embedding) or at a uniformly drawn step; `grad_last` -> `grad_step=k`, same cost. Optionally align every step (cost of A).

findings.title: The note's 'ranking realized?' and 'representation probe' evaluations are not yet covered: all reported accuracies are in-sample for the head
findings.detail: rank/acc_shaped (0.65-0.82) is computed on the same 1,816 training captions the head is fitted on, 16 visits each. probe_heldout.py supports --head but only identity-head probes exist (probe/jobs.txt: base, hp1_naive_s0, hp1_ours_s0). My CPU check on the saved heads finds NO per-anchor memorisation signature (1-cos(g(u),u) is 0.198/0.195/0.193 on anchors seen by the head, 3k anchors never seen, and 4,000 held-out 118k anchors; B1 step 2000), which is encouraging, but generalisation of the ORDERING and transfer to true DINO (rgb_g) are untested.
findings.evidence: phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1435 (acc on training captions), phaseW/rank/probe/jobs.txt, checkpoints .../151302/rank_head_step{500..2000}.pt exist unused; REVIEW_CONTEXT 'pairwise accuracy in the shaped projector space 0.65 (B1) ... 0.69 (A)'.
findings.consequence: Nothing yet shows the shaped space is prompt-aware rather than fitted; the campaign's mechanistic endpoint is missing.
findings.fix: Run probe.lsf now with CKPT=checkpoint_step2000.pt HEAD=rank_head_step2000.pt for B1 s0 (and step1000 for A s0): 1 GPU, ~1 s/caption. Add to the probe: a shuffled-anchor space (F3), per-caption saved embeddings, and a linear probe / AUC of margins on held-out pairs.

findings.title: Degenerate solution is real: the head can (and in A does) satisfy the ranking with an anchor-independent 'shared photo direction'
findings.detail: Because one u_ref anchors all m prompts and g is applied to both sides, g can raise R for 'positive-typical' generations against ANY photo by adding a shared component to real-photo embeddings and typical generations; negatives are systematically atypical prompts (purple trains, 'far from', 'under a slope'). Test on the replay set (2,000 captions x 4 teacher candidates, true DINO): cosine of a generation to an UNRELATED photo rises under A's step-1000 head from 0.115 (raw) to 0.264, own-photo gap shrinks 0.394 -> 0.347, AUC(own>other) 0.974 -> 0.951, mean-embedding norm 0.37 -> 0.55, PC1 share 0.063 -> 0.100; anchor-anchor mean cosine 0.14 -> 0.30. B1's head does the opposite (cross-cosine 0.11 -> 0.04, whitening) but re-orders the same-prompt candidates that the selection ranked (argmax agreement with raw DINO 1.00 -> 0.74 at step 2000; A: 0.73).
findings.evidence: CPU analysis of checkpoints/phaseW/phaseW_CD_dinop_hard_3k-rewRi-s16-rankA-hp1-acc4_s0_151316/rank_head_step1000.pt and .../151302/rank_head_step{500,1000,1500,2000}.pt against phaseW/latent_scorer/replay_2k.pt (e_cand, e_ref) and ref_emb_3k/118k.pt; rank_utils.py:36 (both sides normalised through the same residual MLP), trainer 1400.
findings.consequence: In A, 43% of the shaped reward of any generation (0.264/0.611) is anchor-independent vs 23% raw: acc_shaped and the shaped reward partly measure 'looks like a typical positive rollout', not agreement with the photo; the student is then rewarded for typicality. B1's head changes which same-prompt candidate is best, so the reward space and the selection space disagree.
findings.fix: (i) Shuffled-anchor control in training logs and in the probe (score rollouts against another caption's g(u_ref); shaped acc must fall to ~0.5); (ii) shuffled-negatives / random-positive control for the head; (iii) remove the shared direction explicitly (centre embeddings with a running mean before g, or use a difference-based reward R_j - mean_k R_k); (iv) apply g to the generation side only, keeping u_ref fixed, which removes the 'move the photo' degree of freedom.

findings.title: Variant A's gradient contains a destructive direction: it trains the student to generate edited (CompBench-like) prompts WORSE
findings.detail: For the softmax-contrastive loss, dL/dR_j = p_j/kappa > 0 for every negative: theta is pushed to move the rollouts of 'a purple train' / 'three zebras' AWAY from the real photo. Rendering the edit faithfully and rendering garbage both lower R_j, and no term supervises the negatives' quality (CD supervises only the COCO caption). The only guard is an 8-caption raw-DINO monitor every 100 updates (values 0.29-0.96, acknowledged uninformative). Negatives are precisely the attribute/count/relation edits T2I-CompBench and GenEval score.
findings.evidence: phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1405-1416 (backprop through P and 4 steps, loss on all m), rank_utils.py:85-88; A s0 log: rank_loss 1.05 -> 0.72-0.77, margin_shaped +0.007 -> +0.13-0.15 by step 1000 (B1's head-only margin is 0.03-0.06), so the student is moving the rollouts; rank ratio 0.52-0.89 of the CD gradient at step 1000 (151316).
findings.consequence: A can degrade exactly the prompt family the benchmarks measure, or exploit P's blind spots on negatives (P never sees edited-prompt generations), while acc_shaped looks excellent.
findings.fix: Log, every 100 updates on >=64 captions (decode 60 ms/img): VQAScore or CLIP of each negative rollout vs its own prompt, DINO(neg rollout, pos rollout), and a fixed image panel to wandb. Ablations: stop-gradient on the negatives' rollouts (push only the positive), or a hinge with margin so satisfied pairs stop contributing.

findings.title: B1/A's shaped reward is a 2-4x larger and increasingly CD-opposed gradient than the reference reward: a magnitude confound, not a shape effect
findings.detail: lambda=80 was set for a ~20% share at step 0 with g = identity. As the head's residual grows (||fc2.W|| 2.8 -> 6.5, ||g(u)-u|| 0.35 -> 0.62, B1) the cosine's Jacobian through g grows with it. Reward-probe ratios (||grad reward||/||grad CD||): B1 0.25-0.33 at 0, 0.60-0.97 at 1000, 0.40-1.93 at 1500, 0.76-1.58 at 2000 with cos(CD, reward) -0.63..-0.81; A at 1000: 0.92-1.17 plus the rank term 0.52-0.89. The 2x8 'ours' s2 (151361) stays at 0.15-0.48 (500) and 0.23-0.44 (1000). With clip=1 always active, the reward's share of the normalised update is 2-4x the reference's.
findings.evidence: logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151302.out and -151316.out '[reward-probe]' lines at steps 1000/1500/2000; logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151361.out at 500/1000; head norms from rank_head_step*.pt; the reference 145176 has no probe lines.
findings.consequence: B1 vs ours differs in reward magnitude and direction, not only in prompt-awareness; any B1 effect (or CD-loss / fidelity regression) cannot be attributed to the ranking.
findings.fix: Normalise the shaped reward's gradient to the raw reward's (rescale lambda by the running ratio of ||grad_shaped||/||grad_raw|| on the probe params), or freeze g after a pretraining stage (F9); add a control 'ours with lambda_reward matched to B1's realised share'.

findings.title: Minimal detectable effect (~0.045-0.09 CompBench) is far above the effects at play, and seed pairing is broken for seeds 1-2
findings.detail: n=3 seeds, per-model noise ~0.01-0.02 (averaged checkpoints), sigma_d ~0.014-0.028; a paired t-test with df=2 needs d ~ 3.1 sigma_d for 80% power -> MDE 0.045-0.09, versus ours-naive of +0.0017 on this schedule (+0.015 on the old one). Seeds 1-2 controls (151349/151357/151361/151403) run 2 GPUs x accum 8 while B1/A s1,s2 run 4x4 (and B2 s0 runs 2x8 vs ours s0 4x4): DistributedSampler shards, per-rank micro counters, Delta draws and rollout noise all differ, so only B1 s0 and A s0 share their data order with ours s0 (same target_map_sha256 dbd0d57b...). Prompt-level paired tests compare two specific models, not the treatment.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank_jobs.txt, phaseW/hp1_jobs.txt (acc8 vs acc4 dirs), trainer 746-751 (sampler by world size), 607 (delta_rng per rank), rank_utils.py:163-166 (noise keyed by rank, micro); pairing hashes in logs 151302/151316/145176 (dbd0d57b) vs 145172/151349 (35d2d955, naive uses a different map by design).
findings.consequence: CompBench/GenEval2 cannot decide the hypothesis at realistic effect sizes; a null is uninformative and a 'significant' prompt-level result may be seed noise.
findings.fix: Run s1/s2 controls at 4x4 (or the arms at 2x8) so each arm is data-order-paired with its control; pre-register a mixed model (prompt-paired, seed as random effect) and treat CompBench as secondary; make the held-out ranking transfer (rgb_g on 1,000 captions, per family) the primary endpoint.

findings.title: kappa=0.1 on 0.01-0.05 spreads puts the loss in its linear regime; the note's kappa->inf sanity check is vacuous under Adam
findings.detail: Logits differ by 0.1-0.5, so softmax is near-uniform and L ~ log m - (R_1 - mean R_j)/kappa (B1 loss 1.05 -> 0.88 ~ log 2.2). kappa only rescales the head's gradient, which AdamW (scale-invariant) and the clip at 1.0 undo, so the head's trajectory is essentially kappa-independent; for the student's term kappa->inf just equals lambda_rank->0. There is also no hard-pair focus: already-correct pairs keep pushing their margins, which is what inflates the head's residual (F5).
findings.evidence: rank_utils.py:85-88; trainer 890 (AdamW lr 1e-4), 1460 (clip 1.0); '[rank] step' loss/margin values in logs 151302/151316; probe margins: latent sd 0.030, 38% of pairs within 0.01.
findings.consequence: 'kappa -> infinity recovers the baseline' would not hold as stated; the effective objective is a plain unbounded margin.
findings.fix: kappa ~ within-caption spread (0.01-0.02) or per-caption standardised rewards; or a hinge with margin. Use shuffled-negatives / shuffled-anchor / identity-head (= ours, exists) as the nulls instead of kappa->inf.

findings.title: Ranking in the latent-projector space discards most of the edit signal before the head sees it
findings.detail: P was trained to rank same-prompt teacher candidates (cosine + KL over 4 candidates) and is refreshed on positive-caption predictions plus teacher replay; it never sees an edited-prompt generation. Held-out probe: latent 0.499 (base) / 0.538 (naive) / 0.537 (ours) vs rgb 0.565 / 0.606 / 0.627; latent margin 0.0025-0.0045 vs rgb 0.015-0.022; 21% of latent pairs within 0.005 and 38% within 0.01 (rgb: 9%/17%). In-training acc_raw hovers 0.52-0.60.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/probe/{base,hp1_naive_s0,hp1_ours_s0}.json summaries; trainer 1505-1528 (refresh set = rbuf positives + replay); README mapping row 'DINO features of a generation'.
findings.consequence: The head must manufacture prompt-awareness from a near-chance signal, and P's refresh keeps optimising for a distribution that excludes the negatives, so P-space and RGB-space orderings can diverge unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add the decoded rollouts (positive + negatives, already decoded by the monitor) to the refresh set with their true DINO embeddings, and/or train g on true DINO features of decoded rollouts every k updates (the note's f(x0_hat)).

findings.title: Head trained jointly from step 0 makes B1/A's reward a moving target and departs from the note's staged recipe
findings.detail: The note: train g on the partial order, confirm ranking climbs and the space separates, THEN enable transfer. Here g starts at identity and changes every update while the student optimises <g(P(x0_hat)), g(u_ref)>; the shaped reward drifts down (0.43 -> 0.34) while the raw score rises like the reference, i.e. the student chases a space that is being reshaped under it. The final model is a co-adaptation, not 'ours + a prompt-aware space'. Also g is applied in the reward to one-step x0_hat at sigma 0.34-0.69 (K=8 sigmas for states 4..7 minus Delta) although it is fitted only on rollout endpoints.
findings.consequence: Confounds F5 and makes B1's effect hard to interpret as representation transfer.
findings.fix: Pretrain g on no-grad rollouts of the ours checkpoint (0.27 s/caption -> ~8 min per pass over 1,816 captions on 1 GPU), verify it on the held-out probe, freeze it, then run B1/A with the fixed g; keep the joint version as a secondary arm.

findings.title: A large share of negatives are weakly contradicted or implausible, violating the O1 validity condition
findings.detail: Spatial: 358/541 (66%) are 'far from' ('a street sign far from buildings', 'a frame attached to a wall far from a kitchen'), which a photo rarely contradicts and the model rarely renders; 18 'under/below + surface noun' escape the filter ('riding skis under a snow covered slope', 'under a body of water', 'grazing under a grass covered field'). Verbs: 385/675 standing<->sitting and 121 holding->dropping (a still of dropping looks like holding). Counts: 452/631 are two -> three/four/five, which DINO patch-mean barely resolves. Colour (1,236) is the best-formed family.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/negatives_3k.json counts; phaseW/rank/build_negatives.py:276-282 (surface check only on the word right after the article/one adjective), PAIRS['spatial'] mapping next to/near -> far from.
findings.consequence: Near-tie pairs (17% of rgb pairs within 0.01) are label noise for g and, in A, pressure to make synonymous prompts diverge; per-family conclusions for spatial/verb/count are weak.
findings.fix: Drop 'far from' (or use left/right swaps only); extend the surface filter to any SURFACE noun in the object NP; weight or filter pairs by an offline contradiction score (VQAScore of the photo vs the negative caption, computed once); report families separately.

findings.title: Held-out probe overlaps the projector's training captions
findings.detail: probe_heldout.py excludes only the 3k pool (by prompt and reference; all 3,000 are present in the 118k cache so the exclusion works). The projector's train/val captions (22,000 + 2,000, phaseW/latent_scorer/manifest.jsonl 'split') and the replay set come from the same 118k cache and are not excluded, so ~21% of the 300 probe captions were P-training captions whose e_ref entered P's KL term. Affects latent/latent_g only; rgb/rgb_g and the students (trained on 3k) are clean.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/probe_heldout.py:75-77; manifest split counts train 22000 / val 2000 / test 3000.
findings.consequence: latent-space probe numbers are mildly optimistic for P.
findings.fix: Exclude prompts with manifest split in {train, val}; keep the same seeded draw so existing base/naive/ours probes stay comparable after re-running.

findings.title: Probe size makes per-family and between-model differences unreadable
findings.detail: 833 pairs over 300 captions: 3d_spatial 27 pairs, shape 79, texture 81, spatial 97 (SE 0.05-0.10 per family). The overall naive-vs-ours rgb difference is +0.023 with a paired per-caption SE of 0.020 (n.s.). Ties count as failures and margins are not reported per family.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/probe/hp1_ours_s0.json summary n_pairs; paired per-caption computation on hp1_naive_s0/hp1_ours_s0 records.
findings.consequence: The endpoint that should carry the verdict (F6) cannot resolve realistic changes.
findings.fix: n=1,000-2,000 captions (~1 s/caption), paired per-caption differences with bootstrap CIs, AUC of margins, and per-family margins.

findings.title: No effective anti-hacking monitor for the negatives' branch
findings.detail: rank/acc_rgb uses rank 0's last 8 captions (~10 pairs, SE ~0.15) every 100 updates; the reward-path hacking monitor (rgb_proj_corr) covers only positive predictions. Nothing measures whether negative rollouts stay faithful images or whether P's ordering on them matches true DINO.
findings.evidence: trainer 1437-1440 (rank_buf capped at 16, is_main only), 1465-1477 (rank_buf[-8:]); log values 0.417/0.917/0.458/0.792.
findings.consequence: P-space hacking on the negatives (A) or drift between P and RGB orderings goes unnoticed.
findings.fix: Buffer rollouts from all ranks (gather z_K) and decode >=64 captions per reading (~15 s), log acc_rgb, acc_rgb_shaped, RGB-vs-P rank correlation on negatives, and DINO(neg, pos) similarity.

findings.title: B1's transfer channel (the reward) is inert on the converged schedule
findings.detail: B1 differs from ours only in the reward's metric; on this schedule ours-naive is +0.0017 (1 seed), i.e. the channel B1 relies on currently produces no measurable effect. A perfectly prompt-aware g acting through an inert channel cannot show on CompBench.
findings.evidence: REVIEW_CONTEXT 'converged schedule (1 seed): naive 0.4860, ours 0.4877'; launch_rank.sh EXTRA[B1] (only --rank_shaped_reward added).
findings.consequence: A B1 null is expected regardless of the hypothesis.
findings.fix: Confirm the reward channel is live first (the constant-LR schedule where ours-naive = +0.015, p 0.004), or run B1 there; otherwise judge B1 by the representation endpoints.

findings.title: Additional metrics and controls that would make the test decisive
findings.detail: (1) Shuffled-anchor and shuffled-negatives nulls (cheap, offline on saved embeddings) instead of kappa->inf. (2) Per-family CompBench mapping is direct: color->color, shape->shape, texture->texture, spatial->spatial, 3d_spatial->3D-spatial, count->numeracy; verbs have no CompBench counterpart (use GenEval2 action/relation atoms). (3) VQAScore of the negatives' rollouts vs their own prompt as ground truth of contradiction and as the F4 guard. (4) Kendall tau is n/a for the partial order; use AUC of margins and pos-vs-neg DINO similarity to quantify ties. (5) Train g on true DINO features of decoded rollouts (F8). (6) Hard-negative mining only after F10's filtering, otherwise it mines nonsense. (7) LLM negatives would fix coverage (61%) and the 'far from' problem at modest cost (3k captions, one call each). (8) A gradient-cosine log between the raw and shaped reward gradients w.r.t. x0_hat would show directly how much g changes the reward's direction.
findings.evidence: REVIEW_CONTEXT question 4; F3/F4/F7/F10 above.
findings.consequence: Without (1) and (3) the two degenerate solutions cannot be excluded; without (2) per-family claims are unsupported.
findings.fix: Implement (1), (3) and (8) before the arms finish; they read only saved embeddings/rollouts.

findings.title: Minor deviations that are justified or cosmetic
findings.detail: Full 4-step rollouts instead of the one-step surrogate: justified (on-policy, matches the eval sampler, and is the note's 'few-step differentiable sampler' option); the bf16 casts between steps are differentiable. DINOv2-B and the 1024-wide residual head: fine. 'Both sides through g' is not a deviation: the note's eq. (3) is cos(g(f(x_hat)), g(f_bar)). Partial order is the note's recommended start. 'checkpoint_avg_last5.pt' averages 3 checkpoints (2000/2500/final) and carries step 3000 so the EVAL_MIN_STEP gate passes; naming only.
findings.evidence: DESIGN_NOTE.tex lines 34-38, 50; rank_utils.py:69-82; phaseW/average_checkpoints.py:43-44; launch_rank.sh:44-45.
findings.consequence: None.
findings.fix: Correct REVIEW_CONTEXT's 'both sides through g' from 'deviation' to 'as in the note'; note the 3-member average in the label.

validated: Gradient paths are as claimed: the head is trained only by _l_head on detached embeddings (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1400-1402); the student's ranking term in A and the shaped reward use torch.func.functional_call with detached head parameters (rank_utils.py:39-45; trainer 1256, 1406), so the student never trains g and g never receives student gradient; the B2 align target is detached (1421).

DDP parity: head and align projector are seeded identically and broadcast at init (887-896), their grads are all-reduced (mean), clipped at 1.0 and stepped once per update on every rank (1457-1464); every rank runs the same number of grad-enabled DDP forwards per micro-step (rollouts run even for captions without negatives, 1391-1394); multiple grad forwards before one backward is valid with find_unused_parameters=False and non-reentrant checkpointing (transformer_sd3.py:416 use_reentrant=False); A s0 has run >1,000 updates without a DDP error.

RNG isolation: head/align init happens under a saved-and-restored global RNG state (884-898); rollout noise comes from a private generator keyed by (seed, rank, micro) (rank_utils.py:163-166); encode_prompt/decoding consume no RNG. The pairing hash target_map_sha256 of B1 s0, A s0 and B2 s0 equals the reference ours s0 (145176: dbd0d57b...), so the 4x4 arms share caption order, Delta draws and selection with ours s0.

Scheduler state: rollout_schedule restores the K=8 schedule (rank_utils.py:48-55) and rollout_states calls set_timesteps(K) on every visit (trainer 59) before the CD branch reads timesteps (1075); the 4-step sigmas [1.0, 0.858, 0.602, 0.009, 0] are the pipeline's own 4-step schedule used by the eval and the probe.

The latent projector L2-normalises its output (train_projector.py:50) and u_ref is unit-norm, so both the raw reward and the shaped reward are true cosines; with g = identity (zero-init fc2) and lambda_rank = 0 the trainer is bit-identical in loss to 'ours' by construction.

Head/align optimizer accumulation is correct: losses are divided by accum per micro-step, grads accumulate over the window, are all-reduced, clipped and stepped once per update, then zeroed (1402, 1460-1464).

Checkpoint/hook interplay in B2: the forward hook adds no parameters, so student state_dicts are unchanged; rank_head_step*.pt saves the head and align_proj with the rank_/align_ args (1665-1668, 1679-1682); average_checkpoints.py stamps the latest member step so EVAL_MIN_STEP=3000 passes.

AlignHook reads the right stream: diffusers 0.32.2 JointTransformerBlock.forward returns (encoder_hidden_states, hidden_states), so out[-1] is the image-token stream; block 8 of 24 is not the context_pre_only last block; the hook is registered after the teacher deepcopy so the teacher is unaffected; features() asserts the captured activation carries grad.

The shaped reward is implemented as specified: <g(P(x0_hat)), g(u_ref)> with g's weights detached on the two least-noisy supervised predictions (1245-1259), replacing the raw cosine only when --rank_shaped_reward is set; args.json of B1/A/B2 match the launcher (B2 has rank_shaped_reward False, align_lambda 60).
lambda calibration reproduces: the smoke's weight-1 ratios (rank 0.07-0.35, align 0.0036-0.005 of the CD gradient) become 0.09-0.46 and 0.22-0.33 at step 0 in the live runs with 1.3 / 60.

Probe held-out selection excludes the 3k pool by both prompt text and reference path, and all 3,000 pool prompts/references are found in the 118k cache, so the exclusion is effective; the identity-head spaces latent_g/rgb_g reproduce latent/rgb exactly (probe/*.json), confirming the head path; noise is seeded by caption idx so models are compared paired.

The saved heads show no per-anchor memorisation: 1-cos(g(u),u) is identical on anchors the head saw (1,816), 3k anchors it never saw (1,184) and 4,000 held-out 118k anchors (0.198/0.195/0.193 at B1 step 2000; 0.326/0.320/0.321 at A step 1000).

negatives_3k.json matches the README (1,816/3,000 captions, 929/210/677 with 3/2/1 negatives, 3,884 negatives; families color 1,236, verb 675, count 631, spatial 541, shape 382, texture 286, 3d 133) and the rule set in build_negatives.py implements the audited constraints (attributive colour, numeral 'one' with pluralisation, size antonyms, material classes, animate-subject verbs, surface-noun filter for 'on top of').

Both sides through g and the partial-order loss are faithful to DESIGN_NOTE.tex (eq. 3 and the recommended softmax-contrastive simplification); full differentiable rollouts are one of the two paths the note allows for Variant A.
lenses.summary: Section-by-section, the code does what README claims and the plumbing is sound (gradient paths, DDP parity, RNG isolation, scheduler, optimizer accumulation, checkpoints all verified; no code bug found). The problems are in the mapping from the note to the experiment. (1) B2's REPA term hooks the last rollout step at sigma=0.009, so it regresses block-8 features onto the shaped embedding of an essentially identical clean latent: an autoencoding task that reaches none of the composition-deciding steps; a B2 result is uninformative about the note's Variant B (fix: hook the first step). (2) The note's 'ranking realized?' and 'representation probe' are not yet covered: every reported accuracy is in-sample for the head; the trained heads have not been run on the held-out probe although checkpoints exist. (3) The degenerate solution is real and measurable: with a shared anchor and g on both sides, g can raise rewards via a shared 'photo direction'; A's step-1000 head raises the shaped cosine between a generation and an UNRELATED photo from 0.115 to 0.264 and compresses the anchor cloud (mean anchor cosine 0.14 -> 0.30), while B1's head whitens instead but re-orders 26% of same-prompt candidates that the selection ranked; shuffled-anchor and shuffled-negative controls are required. (4) A's loss pushes negatives' rollouts away from the photo with nothing guarding their quality, i.e. it can train the student to generate CompBench-style edited prompts worse; the 8-caption RGB monitor cannot see this. (5) The shaped reward's gradient share grows to 0.8-1.9x the CD gradient with cos(CD, reward) down to -0.8, versus 0.2-0.45 for the raw reward in 'ours', so B1 vs ours is confounded by reward magnitude; freeze g after a pretraining stage or normalise its gradient. (6) Statistically the CompBench plan cannot decide anything: MDE ~0.045-0.09 at 3 seeds versus effects of 0.002-0.015, and seeds 1-2 controls run 2x8 while the arms run 4x4, breaking the data-order pairing that exists only for seed 0. Further: kappa=0.1 puts the loss in a linear regime where kappa->inf is vacuous under Adam; P-space discards most of the edit signal (latent probe ~0.50-0.54 vs rgb 0.57-0.63) and P is never refreshed on edited-prompt generations; 66% of spatial negatives are 'far from', 18 are 'under a slope/water' nonsense, verbs are dominated by standing/sitting and holding/dropping. Path verdict: the head-shaping idea is testable, but as instrumented the campaign will produce numbers that cannot distinguish prompt-awareness from typicality shortcuts, reward-magnitude confounds and seed noise. What would change my mind: a trained head that lifts held-out rgb_g pairwise accuracy above rgb (per family, n>=1,000 captions, paired CIs) while shuffled-anchor accuracy stays at chance, VQAScore of negatives' rollouts not decreasing in A, and B1/A vs ours compared at matched reward-gradient share with data-order-paired seeds.

findings.title: The dominant families' O1 labels are at chance in the space the head operates on
findings.detail: The ranking label (positive rollout closer to the COCO photo than the negative's rollout) is only usable if the scorer can register the edit. In the probe's raw RGB DINO space, object-colour negatives (277 of 293 colour pairs; colour is 32% of training negatives) order at 0.47 (base), 0.55 (naive), 0.57 (ours); count |delta|=1 (55% of count negatives: 347/631) at 0.51/0.56/0.52; size antonyms 0.56/0.61/0.61; 'far from' 0.63/0.60/0.63. The only strong signals are whole-scene edits: colour on sky/water/grass nouns 0.88/0.81/0.94 (n=16), texture 0.77/0.78/0.74, posture verbs 0.63/0.65/0.73, count |delta|=3 0.85/0.69/0.77. Some object-colour pairs are anti-ordered (base red->green acc 0.22, margin -0.051, n=18; red->blue 0.37): recolouring an object toward the background palette moves a patch-MEAN embedding toward the photo. A single-word local edit barely moves a global cosine (median |pos-neg| 0.03 against a positive score of 0.6), so the label is dominated by everything the caption does not mention.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/probe/{base,hp1_naive_s0,hp1_ours_s0}.json records, sliced per (family, source, target) and per noun class; phaseW/rank/build_negatives.py summary (families); probe_heldout.py:132-133 (patch-mean cosine).
findings.consequence: For roughly half of the negatives the head g is fitted to labels that are noise or anti-correlated in P/DINO space; the shortcut that satisfies them is 'match the photo's global colour/texture statistics', not attribute binding. A positive result on B1/A would not show prompt-awareness without the controls in N15/N16; a null would not refute the hypothesis (label noise).
findings.fix: (a) Drop or down-weight families whose raw rgb accuracy is <0.6 on the probe (object colour on small nouns, count +-1, far from, size on rooms/persons); (b) build the label with a region-aware score (max/top-k over DINO patch-pair cosines between generation and photo, or the mean over the patches that changed between positive and negative rollouts) so a local edit is visible; (c) check per negative that the photo contradicts it with VQAScore(photo, negative) < VQAScore(photo, positive) before it enters training (N15).

findings.title: COCO captions cannot supply 'compositional rearrangements'; what was built are single-attribute substitutions
findings.detail: The design note's validity condition is 'compositional rearrangements of the same objects (attribute swaps, spatial swaps, count changes over the same nouns)'. Every negative in negatives_3k.json changes ONE span to a new value; none swaps attributes between two nouns or reverses a relation's arguments. The 3k pool offers almost no material for real swaps: 53 captions with two distinct attributive colours, 4 with two counts, 13 mentioning left/right, 192 with on top of/under/above/below (argument swap possible). Left/right, the CompBench 2D-spatial staple, appears 0 times among 541 spatial negatives; 66% of spatial negatives are next to/near -> far from (358), a distance relation that a still photo barely contradicts; true shape edits are 17 of 3,884 (0.4%), the 'shape' family being 96% size antonyms (365/382).
findings.evidence: negatives_3k.json family/source/target counts; counts of swap-capable captions over phaseN/coco_selection_dinopatch; PAIRS['spatial'] in phaseK/build_counterfactuals.py:39.
findings.consequence: The negatives test attribute substitution (which a bag-of-visual-words scorer can solve by histogram matching), not binding or relation structure; a per-family CompBench mapping would have colour and texture covered, shape and 2D-spatial (left/right) essentially uncovered, non-spatial covered only through verbs.
findings.fix: Either accept and rename the claim (attribute-substitution-aware, not compositional), or source negatives from prompts that admit swaps: CompBench-style two-attribute prompts with their own anchors (escalation path ii), or synthesise binding negatives on the 53/192 swap-capable captions and weight them up; add argument swaps for 'X on top of Y' -> 'Y on top of X' (192 captions) which keep the global palette fixed and defeat the histogram shortcut.

findings.title: Surface-noun skip for 'on top of' fires only when the surface noun ends the caption (greedy regex)
findings.detail: build_negatives.py:279 matches an optional article, then an OPTIONAL single adjective `(?:[A-Za-z']+[\s-]+)?`, then the noun. The adjective group is greedy, so whenever a word follows the noun it consumes the noun and the SURFACE test is applied to the next word. Direct test: 'on top of a hill in the day' -> checks 'in'; 'on top of a snow covered slope' -> checks 'covered'; 'on top of a field next to a dog' -> checks 'next' (not skipped), while 'on top of a field' (end of caption) is skipped. 15 of the 114 on top of->under negatives place the subject under a slope/hill/beach/body of water ('A man riding a snowboard under a snow covered slope', 'A ram sitting under a hill in the day', 'A little girl flying a kite under a lush green field').
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/build_negatives.py:276-281; regex test output; 15 matching negatives in negatives_3k.json.
findings.consequence: 13% of the strongest spatial sub-family are nonsense prompts whose rollouts are arbitrary; the README claim 'not on top of a field -> under' is only true for caption-final nouns.
findings.fix: Replace the regex with a window test: `if set(_words(prompt[m.end():])[:4]) & SURFACE: continue` (any of the next 3-4 words a surface noun), and apply the same window to 'under'/'below' -> 'above' edits (truck above a tree, sink above a mirror).

findings.title: Verb rule is 'any animate token anywhere before the verb', not 'animate subject'; group/couple/teddy bear leak paraphrases
findings.detail: build_negatives.py:264-266 tests `set(_words(prompt[:m.start()])) & ANIMATE`. ANIMATE (line 92) contains 'group', 'couple', 'crowd', 'family' and food/toy-ambiguous animals ('bear', 'chicken', 'turkey', 'fish', 'lamb'). Results: 12 negatives whose only animate token is group/couple over inanimate nouns ('A group of umbrellas is sitting -> standing', 'A couple of white chairs sitting -> standing', 'A group of motorcycles ... sitting -> standing', 'A group of wooden benches sitting -> standing', 'A couple of pieces of luggage sitting -> standing'); 19 teddy/stuffed/toy cases ('A brown teddy bear sitting on a train -> standing'); 120/675 (18%) verb edits have a non-animate nearest content word, of which by inspection roughly a third attach the verb to an object ('A cat laying on luggage sitting on the floor' -> luggage standing). For objects, COCO's 'sitting' means 'located' and 'standing' is a paraphrase: the photo does NOT contradict it.
findings.evidence: negatives_3k.json verb rows; ANIMATE set at build_negatives.py:92-106; audit_negatives.py:44-45 uses the same any-token test, so it reports 1 hit (0.03%) and cannot see these.
findings.consequence: ~3-5% of verb negatives (about 1% of all) are paraphrases that teach the wrong order; small in count but they carry no contradiction and the head cannot satisfy them.
findings.fix: Require the head noun of the NP immediately before the verb to be animate: walk back over adjectives/'that is'/'are' to the nearest content word; treat 'group/couple/crowd/family/herd of X' by testing X; drop 'teddy'/'stuffed'/'toy'-preceded animals; blacklist 'plate/bowl/piece of <animal>'.

findings.title: Half of the within-caption negative pairs edit the same span; 387 captions have all three negatives on one word
findings.detail: The round-robin in negatives_for (build_negatives.py:318-329) takes one edit per family per round, so a caption whose only editable word is a colour gets three colours of that word ('A big airplane flying in the big blue sky' -> green sky, yellow sky, and 'small airplane'). 1,478 of 2,997 within-caption pairs (49%) share (family, span); 387 of 1,139 multi-negative captions have every negative on the same span; only 159 captions cover 3 families and 1,145 cover 1.
findings.evidence: negatives_3k.json; counts computed over all captions with >=2 negatives.
findings.consequence: With the partial-order softmax (ranking_loss, kappa 0.1) three same-span negatives triple the weight of one contrast instead of adding compositional diversity; the effective number of distinct contrasts is ~2,400 not 3,884, and per-family probe accuracies over pooled pairs weight such captions 3x.
findings.fix: Prefer a new span, then a new family, before a second target of the same span; cap same-span negatives at 1 unless nothing else exists, or weight each negative by 1/(number of negatives sharing its span) in the loss.

findings.title: About 10% of negatives are nonsense prompts and ~28% are only weakly contradicted (sample of 215)
findings.detail: Judged over a stratified sample of 215 (25 per family + 40 random). Nonsense (contradicted, but the rollout is arbitrary): texture 7/27 (leather wall, brick plates, fabric plates, leather shelves, 'clear leather bubble umbrellas', 'stainless glass restroom'), spatial 4/34 (kitchen island above track lighting, sink above a mirror, truck above a tree, bikes far from each other on a bike rack), count 3/36 ('Four elephants..., two are babies the other is the parent' - 20 such enumeration inconsistencies in the file), 3d 2/25 (woman behind a mirror taking her picture), verb 4/33 ('dropping a phone in each of his hands'; holding->dropping is 121 negatives = 18% of verbs), colour 2/30 (yellow water, black slices). Weakly contradicted (a still photo cannot refute them): size on rooms/persons/close-ups (~16/30 shape; 'a close up of a small plane -> big plane'), 'far from' (24/34 spatial), walking->running, holding->dropping, playing with->ignoring, six->five donuts, glass<->plastic (17 texture). Clearly compatible/paraphrase: ~5/215 (cabinets below the counter -> above: kitchens have both; 'red cow' for a brown cow; 'big girl/kid' for a little girl (36 such semantic shifts in the file); 'skier farther behind -> farther in front of him'). Grammar is good: article agreement 0 errors, but 13 'AN orange ...' from _case_like on the article (build_negatives.py:299), 1 'two cellulars phone' (line 208-216: the first word not in ADJ_SKIP is taken as the noun), and awkward 'from in front of'.
findings.evidence: Stratified sample printed from negatives_3k.json (seed 2026); counts: holding->dropping 121/675, far from 358/541, glass<->plastic 17/286, big/little on persons 36/382, enumeration inconsistencies 20/631, AN 13, colour compound nouns 23/1236 (orange slices/peels -> black slices, brown bear -> red/blue/green bear, white rice -> blue rice, green beans -> purple beans), 'stainless steel' -> stainless glass/wooden 8/286.
findings.consequence: Nonsense negatives produce the largest margins (their rollouts differ from the photo in every patch), so under kappa 0.1 they dominate the head's gradient and teach 'penalise any weird image'; weak negatives consume a full 4-step rollout each (A arm 8.3 s/update) for near-zero margin (probe: far from 0.60-0.63, count +-1 0.51-0.56, weak verbs 0.53-0.67, size 0.56-0.61).
findings.fix: Rules: material targets by noun class (furniture: wood/metal/plastic/glass; wall/chimney: brick/stone/wood/concrete; plates/cups: paper/plastic/ceramic/glass; leather/fabric only for wearables/seats); add 'stainless' to the compound-prev set (line 246); per-colour following-noun blacklist (orange: slices/peel/juice/tree; brown: bear; white: rice/wine; green: beans/peppers/tea; black: coffee/pepper); skip count edits when the caption enumerates ('one ... one', 'the other'); drop holding->dropping, playing with/feeding->ignoring, walking<->running; keep size edits only on objects with intrinsic scale (buildings, vehicles, animals, waves) and never on person/kid/cat nouns; under/below->above only with a movable subject; for count keep |delta|>=2; capitalise only the first letter of a replaced article.

findings.title: Probe 'held-out' captions overlap the projector's training split: 61 of 300
findings.detail: probe_heldout.py:75-77 excludes only the 3k pool (by prompt and by reference). The projector P was trained on the 22k 'train' split of phaseW/latent_scorer/shards (train 22,000 / val 2,000 / test 3,000); 61 of the 300 probe captions (20%) are in that train split (their u_ref were P's regression targets). The rgb space is unaffected; 'latent' and 'latent_g' are partly in-sample for P.
findings.evidence: phaseW/latent_scorer/shards/shard*.pt 'split'/'prompt' fields vs phaseW/rank/probe/base.json records.
findings.consequence: Latent-space probe numbers (e.g. 3d_spatial latent 0.85 for naive s0, n=20) are not clean held-out estimates; comparisons of latent_g across arms are biased toward captions P has fitted.
findings.fix: Also exclude prompts whose shard split is train or val (and the replay set phaseW/latent_scorer/replay_2k.pt) when building `held` in probe_heldout.py; the 118k minus 3k minus 24k leaves ~87k captions, enough for n=1000.

findings.title: Probe selection (--min_negs 2) and pooled-pair scoring shift the family mix and understate uncertainty
findings.detail: Replicating the probe's draw: 728 held-out captions scanned to reach 300 with >=2 negatives (266 had none = 37%, consistent with the 39% at 3k; 162 single-negative captions were dropped). Dropping them removes mostly verb/spatial/shape captions: with min_negs=1 the same scan gives verb 202 vs 124, spatial 143 vs 97, shape 105 vs 79. Per-family n is small (3d 27 pairs, texture 81) so a family SE is 0.05-0.10; pairs are pooled so 3-negative captions weigh 3x; strict '>' counts ties (|diff|<1e-3: 1.6% rgb, 3.4-5.6% latent) as failures.
findings.evidence: probe_heldout.py:74-86, 141-150; replicated selection with negatives_for on phaseN/coco_selection_118k.
findings.consequence: Family-level differences between arms below ~0.1 (e.g. spatial 0.577 vs 0.629) are within noise; the probe mix does not match training (verb 15% vs 17%, texture 10% vs 7%).
findings.fix: min_negs 1, n=1000 captions, report per-caption mean accuracy with a bootstrap CI over captions and a paired (same caption, same noise) comparison between arms; report the tie rate separately.

findings.title: The uncovered 39% of captions is a biased subset (sports/action/food) that never receives ranking pressure
findings.detail: Covered (1,816) vs uncovered (1,184) word rates: tennis 1.7% vs 3.1%, baseball 0.8% vs 3.0%, pizza 1.2% vs 3.0%, skateboard 0.9% vs 1.5%, person 2.9% vs 4.9%; conversely giraffe 1.9% vs 0.8%, zebra 1.8% vs 0.6%, dog 4.2% vs 2.1%, cat 4.2% vs 1.5%, bear 2.4% vs 0.5%, bed 2.6% vs 0.9%, kite 1.4% vs 0.3%. Covered captions also have a lower cached selection signal (max dino_cos 0.483 vs 0.510). Mean length is similar (10.7 vs 10.1 words).
findings.evidence: phaseN/coco_selection_dinopatch/selection_rank*.jsonl vs negatives_3k.json keys.
findings.consequence: Any per-category interpretation of a CompBench/GenEval2 change must remember the ranking term never touched action/sport/food scenes (the non-spatial-style captions); a gain concentrated on animal/vehicle colour categories would be consistent with the histogram shortcut in N1.
findings.fix: Report CompBench/GenEval2 deltas split by category and, in training logs, the share of updates whose batch caption had negatives; optionally add a cheap family for the uncovered set (e.g. count insertion 'a man' -> 'two men', which the photo contradicts) to raise coverage.

findings.title: Author's audit cannot detect the rule failures above because it re-uses the same heuristics
findings.detail: audit_negatives.py imports ANIMATE and the same any-token test (line 44-45), so it reports 1 verb hit; its colour check flags 52 'A and B noun' edits that are actually fine (e.g. 'a blue and white plate -> green and white plate') and misses compound nouns; it has no check for surface nouns after 'under', enumeration inconsistencies, or nonsense material/noun pairs.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/audit_negatives.py:24-48; run output: 52 colour flags (all first-colour-of-pair edits), 0/0/0/1 elsewhere.
findings.consequence: The '20% flagged -> fixed' narrative in the README understates the residual defect rate (~10% nonsense, ~1-2% paraphrase, ~28% weak in my sample).
findings.fix: Add the checks from N3/N4/N6 and, more usefully, replace heuristic auditing with the VQAScore contradiction test of N15 as the acceptance criterion.

findings.title: Same generator on the 118k cache is consistent, with two caveats
findings.detail: negatives_for is deterministic in the prompt; the 3k prompts are found verbatim in the 118k cache (3000/3000 by prompt and by reference), one caption per photo in both caches (0 shared photos), so the probe's exclusion is sufficient against the 3k pool. Caveats: 1,705 of 113,948 118k prompts carry leading/trailing/double spaces (51 in the 3k), which the rules tolerate; and the family mix is shifted by --min_negs (N8).
findings.evidence: Replicated negatives_for over the 118k cache; whitespace counts.
findings.consequence: No inconsistency in the rules themselves; the probe's negatives share every defect of the training negatives, so it cannot detect label noise.
findings.fix: None needed beyond N7/N8.

findings.title: Measure contradiction and edit-realisation directly with VQAScore (cheap, decisive)
findings.detail: For each of the 3,884 negatives compute VQAScore(photo, positive caption) - VQAScore(photo, negative) with the vendored t2v_metrics: a non-positive gap identifies compatible/paraphrase negatives per family, and the gap size ranks families by how strongly the photo contradicts them. Second, on the probe's rollouts compute VQAScore(negative's generation, negative prompt) vs VQAScore(negative's generation, positive prompt): this measures whether the student even renders the edit (at w=1, 4 steps, prompt adherence is weak), separating 'label unattainable' from 'scorer blind'. Cost: ~7.8k + ~1.7k VQAScore calls, tens of minutes on one GPU.
findings.evidence: REVIEW_CONTEXT.md Q4 lists this; probe median |pos-neg| 0.03 and per-pair accuracies show the need.
findings.consequence: Turns the 'are the negatives sound' question into a measured per-family table and gives a principled filter for the next negatives file.
findings.fix: Run once on the existing negatives_3k.json and the probe JSONs; gate families by mean gap and realisation rate.

findings.title: Controls that separate 'same-object compositional' from 'any-difference' effects
findings.detail: (a) Shuffled negatives: give each caption another caption's negatives (different objects) - if the head/B1/A gains are unchanged the O1 same-object premise did no work; (b) kappa -> infinity (flat) and an argmin arm (train the head/students to rank the positive LAST) bracket the effect; (c) histogram-matched negatives: colour swaps between two nouns (53 captions) and argument swaps of 'on top of' (192 captions) keep the global palette fixed and directly test binding; (d) train the head on true DINO features of decoded rollouts as well as P(z_K) (the rgb_g probe space), since P collapses within-prompt differences (latent median |diff| 0.015 vs rgb 0.03-0.045, tie rate 3-6%).
findings.evidence: probe records; swap-capable caption counts.
findings.consequence: Without (a)-(c) a positive result cannot be attributed to prompt-awareness rather than a colour/texture-matching direction in DINO space.
findings.fix: Each control is one build_negatives variant plus one run per arm; (d) is a flag in the trainer's rank block.

findings.title: Family weighting/expectation for signal
findings.detail: Given the probe, expected carriers of signal under O1 with a patch-mean scorer: texture (0.74-0.78 raw, 7% of negatives), posture verbs standing/sitting/sleeping/lying (0.63-0.73, 57% of verbs), whole-scene colour (sky/water/grass; 0.88-0.94 but only ~5% of colour edits), on top of/under (0.53-0.67), count |delta|>=2 (0.59-0.85), 3D in front of/behind (0.41 base -> 0.63-0.80 trained; n small). Expected null carriers: object colour on small/accessory nouns (118 of 1,236 colour edits are on frisbee/tie/hat/sign/helmet-type nouns), count +-1, far from, size on rooms/persons, holding->dropping, glass<->plastic.
findings.evidence: Per-(family, source, target) accuracies from the probe files; noun-class counts over negatives_3k.json.
findings.consequence: A rebalanced negatives file (drop the null carriers, cap same-span repeats) would spend the same rollout budget on contrasts the scorer can actually see and would raise the head's achievable accuracy above the 0.65-0.69 reported on training captions.
findings.fix: Rebuild with the N6 rules and a family cap (e.g. colour <= 30%, at most one negative per span), then re-run the probe on the base model to confirm raw rgb accuracy >= 0.65 per retained family before training.

validated: Trainer join is correct: negatives_3k.json is keyed by the cache idx and rank_negs.get(int(rec['idx'])) at train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1384 matches the caption; all 1,816 idx->prompt pairs agree with phaseN/coco_selection_dinopatch (0 mismatches); rank_m=3 in every run's args.json, so no family-biased truncation.

No leakage into the 3k pool: 0 negatives equal another 3k caption's positive text (normalised), 0 duplicate captions, 0 photos shared by two captions in either cache; 4 negatives coincide with real 118k captions of other photos, which is harmless under a per-caption anchor.
Probe exclusion of the 3k pool works: all 3,000 pool prompts and references are present in the 118k cache and are excluded by both keys; one caption per photo in the 118k cache.

Grammar: article agreement after the edit is correct in all 3,884 negatives (0 'a <vowel>'/'an <consonant>' introduced); no negative equals its own positive; no duplicate negatives within a caption; no double spaces introduced; 'black and white' is never edited (0) and only 2 edits create that phrase.
The 'one' count rule behaves as documented: 0 pronoun 'one' edits, only 5 'one' edits in the file, all with the noun pluralised (one wrong noun choice, N6).
Family counts, coverage (1,816/3,000 = 60.5%; 929/210/677 with 3/2/1 negatives) and per-family totals in the README/REVIEW_CONTEXT match the file summary exactly.

Colour targets never reuse a colour already in the caption and never fall in the source's near-synonym class (checked via the rotation logic and the audit's 'target already in caption' check: 0 hits).

Size edits are strictly antonyms and shape edits change class (audit: 0 violations); material edits stay material->material and quality edits antonym-only (0 violations); no texture noun edits ('glass of', last word).

The 3d_spatial family is clean by rule: 103 in front of->behind and 30 behind->in front of, only fired when the opposite relation is absent from the caption; in my 25-item sample every one is contradicted by the photo, two are nonsense (behind a mirror).

The probe builds negatives with the identical negatives_for(prompt, m=3) used for training, seeds the shared noise by caption idx, and scores against ref_emb_118k by idx; per-family accuracies in REVIEW_CONTEXT (e.g. ours s0 rgb: 3d 0.63, colour 0.59, count 0.57, shape 0.61, spatial 0.63, texture 0.74, verb 0.70) reproduce from the JSON files.
lenses.summary: The negatives are well-engineered at the rule level (correct idx join, no leakage, articles fixed, families and counts as documented, 3D-spatial and posture-verb edits clean), but they do not deliver what the O1 anchor needs. Two design-level problems dominate: (1) the families that make up most of the file are exactly the ones a patch-mean DINO cosine cannot order - object-colour edits (32% of negatives) are at chance (0.47-0.57 raw rgb) and sometimes anti-ordered (red->green 0.22), count +-1 (55% of count edits) is at 0.51-0.56, 'far from' (66% of spatial) and size antonyms (96% of 'shape') are weakly contradicted at best - while the strong signals are whole-scene edits (texture 0.75, green sky 0.9, standing/sitting 0.65-0.73); and (2) COCO captions cannot supply 'compositional rearrangements': every negative is a single-attribute substitution, zero left/right edits, 17 true-shape edits, only 53 captions with two colours to swap, so the notion tested is attribute substitution that a colour-histogram direction can satisfy. Quantified defects: one real rule bug (surface-noun skip regex is greedy; 15/114 on-top-of->under negatives put people under slopes/hills), the verb 'animate subject' rule is an any-token test (group/couple/teddy-bear paraphrases), ~10% nonsense and ~28% weakly-contradicted negatives in a 215-item stratified sample, 49% of within-caption negative pairs on the same span (387 captions with all three negatives on one word), 23 colour compound nouns, 8 'stainless glass', 13 'AN orange'. Eval-side: 61/300 probe captions sit in the projector's train split, and --min_negs 2 skews the probe mix away from verb/spatial. The uncovered 39% is sports/action/food captions, so the ranking never touches non-spatial scenes. Decisive next steps: VQAScore contradiction and edit-realisation tables per family, a shuffled-negatives control, histogram-preserving swap negatives on the 53/192 swap-capable captions, and a rebuilt file that drops the null-carrier families and caps same-span repeats.

findings.title: B1's shaped reward runs at 2-3x the gradient share of ours' raw reward, so B1-vs-ours confounds geometry with reward strength
findings.detail: The head g amplifies within-caption spread (B1 [rank] lines: margin_shaped 0.03-0.06 vs margin_raw 0.004-0.008), so d<g(P x0_hat), g(u_ref)>/dtheta is larger than the raw reward's gradient at the same lambda=80. The reward probe on the same parameter subset shows the realized reward/CD ratio in B1 far above ours at matched steps, and its cosine to the CD gradient turning strongly negative late in training. With clip=1 always active, the reward's share of the fixed-norm update is what matters, and it is not matched. Prior evidence in phaseW/s4_seed_stats.md (exact reward lambda 7.75 -> 31 -> 62: 0.4910 -> 0.4989 -> 0.5034) shows reward weight alone moves CompBench by ~0.01, i.e. more than the effect this campaign is looking for.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151302.out [reward-probe]: step 1000 ratios 0.80/0.97/0.60/0.76 (mean 0.78); step 1500 0.40/1.93/1.36/0.55 with cos -0.23/-0.70/-0.63/-0.35; step 2000 0.87/2.28/0.76/1.58 with cos +0.82/-0.65/-0.81/-0.04; step 2500 up to 3.23. Ours s2 control /lustre/.../logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151361.out: step 1000 ratios 0.29/0.27/0.23/0.44/0.20/0.15/0.16/0.38 (mean 0.26); step 1500 mean 0.71. Shaped reward code: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1253-1259.
findings.consequence: Whatever B1 shows relative to ours (better or worse) is equally explained by 'stronger, more CD-opposed reward' as by 'prompt-aware geometry'; the contrast does not isolate the hypothesis.
findings.fix: Add a share-matched control: ours with lambda set so its realized reward/CD ratio tracks B1's (~lambda 200-240 from the step-1000 numbers), or renormalize B1's shaped-reward gradient to the raw reward's norm per step (scale lambda by ||grad r_raw||/||grad r_shaped|| measured on probe_params every 50 updates). At minimum, log the realized ratio every 50 updates in every arm and report B1's effect alongside its share trajectory.

findings.title: A's ranking-gradient share is 2.5-4.5x the 20% it was calibrated to; CD is a minority of A's update by step 1000
findings.detail: lambda_rank=1.3 was set from a 6-update smoke with g at identity (rank ratio at weight 1: 0.068-0.35, mean 0.15). As g sharpens (A's margin_shaped 0.006 -> 0.25 by step 1200) the ranking gradient through g and the 4-step chain grows. Together with the shaped reward (F1) the non-consistency terms exceed the CD gradient.
