findings.evidence: Smoke /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/logs/lsf-sd-W-rank-smoke-151298.out [rank-probe] step 0-4 ratios 0.068/0.35/0.089/0.19/0.10/0.12 at lambda 1. Live /lustre/.../logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151316.out step 1000: [rank-probe] ratio 0.89/0.52/0.52 (x lambda 1.3) and [reward-probe] 0.76/1.14/1.17/0.92; [rank] margin_shaped +0.0066 (step 50) -> +0.2480 (step 1200).
findings.consequence: A is running in a regime the design did not intend (ranking + reward ~1.3-2x the CD gradient), so a negative result cannot be read as 'ranking backprop does not help' and a positive one is entangled with the reward-share confound.
findings.fix: Normalize adaptively: every 100 updates set lambda_rank so the probe ratio returns to the target share (or normalize the ranking loss gradient to a fixed fraction of the CD gradient norm). If compute allows, a lambda_rank ladder (0.3 / 1.3) on one seed shows whether the answer depends on the share. Report the realized share trajectory with any A result.

findings.title: Three seeds cannot detect the effect size in play (MDE 0.010-0.026 CompBench, 3-8 GenEval2 points); seed pairing buys nothing
findings.detail: Seed-level SDs of averaged checkpoints in phaseW/s4_seed_stats.md are 0.002-0.010 CompBench and 0.3-1.6 GenEval2 points; seed-paired difference SDs for ours-like contrasts are 0.0021-0.0092. For a paired t-test with n=3 (df=2, alpha 0.05, power 0.8) I computed MDE = 0.0098 / 0.0163 / 0.0261 at sigma_d = 0.003 / 0.005 / 0.008, with 95% CI half-widths 0.0075 / 0.0124 / 0.0199; for GenEval2 sigma_d 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.5 points gives MDE 3.3 / 4.9 / 8.2. The effect of interest is a few thousandths (converged ours-naive = +0.0017; prior GenEval2 +1.0). Pairing does not reduce variance in the existing data: argmax-vs-random paired SD 0.0058 vs unpaired sqrt(0.0032^2+0.0031^2)=0.0045; exact-vs-argmax 0.0062 vs 0.0043 (correlation ~0 or negative).
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/s4_seed_stats.md lines 96-125 (per-seed table) and the seed-paired contrasts table; MDE computed with scipy nct in this review; converged-schedule references /lustre/.../phaseN/eval_W_B2-hp1_3k-hp1-avg_s0_145251/alignment.json (0.4860) and eval_W_CD_dinop_hard-rewRi-s16-hp1_3k-hp1-avg_s0_145253/alignment.json (0.4877).
findings.consequence: A null at n=3 is uninformative below ~0.015 CompBench; any p<0.05 on a few-thousandths effect would be a winner's-curse false positive. The plan can only establish an effect >= ~0.02.
findings.fix: Pre-register one primary contrast (arm minus ours, CompBench mean, averaged checkpoint), report the 95% CI rather than p; treat seeds as independent (Welch), not paired. To reach a few thousandths: 5 seeds -> CI +-0.006, 8 seeds -> +-0.004 at sigma_d 0.005; fund them by dropping the redundant raw-checkpoint evals (F7). Use the held-out ranking probe (with F6 fixes) as the mechanism-level primary, which needs far less compute per unit of power.

findings.title: Prompt-level paired tests: MDE ~0.009 per seed pair, and Wilcoxon disagrees with the t-test on the existing pair
findings.detail: On the existing converged seed-0 pair (ours-avg 145253 vs naive-avg 145251) the per-prompt CompBench difference has SD 0.155 (n=2398), SE 0.0032, mean +0.0017, paired t p=0.59 but Wilcoxon p=0.003; per-category swings between these two runs are -0.027 (spatial) and +0.016 (numeracy). GenEval2 per-prompt diff SD 23 points, SE 0.8 (n=800). So a prompt-level test resolves ~0.009 per seed pair, ~0.005 pooling 3 pairs, but only by treating the checkpoint as fixed (no seed variance), and the asymmetric difference distribution makes a rank test 'significant' where the reported mean metric is flat.
findings.evidence: Computed in this review from per_prompt rows in /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseN/eval_W_*_3k-hp1*_s0_1452{50,51,52,53}/compbench_scores/*/scores.json and geneval2_scores/*/scores.json (eval seeds are per prompt idx, exp0/phaseA_generate.py:137, so cross-model pairing per prompt is valid).
findings.consequence: Choosing the test after seeing the data (t vs Wilcoxon, raw vs avg, pooled vs balanced) can flip the verdict; a prompt-level p-value alone overstates evidence for the method because seed variance is ignored; spatial is the noisiest category (and 31.8% vocabulary-gated), so per-family mapping onto it is underpowered.
findings.fix: Pre-specify the paired t / bootstrap on the mean (the reported metric), category-balanced, pooled over seeds with seed as a cluster (cluster-robust SE or mixed model with seed random effect); never Wilcoxon as primary. Pre-register category contrasts mapped to the negative families (color, numeracy, shape, texture, spatial, 3d_spatial) with non_spatial as a built-in negative control, treated as secondary.

findings.title: World-size mix (2x8 vs 4x4) is a seed-like perturbation, not a batch-composition confound, but it breaks the 'seed-paired' premise for B2 s0 and for naive/ours s1-s2
findings.detail: I verified that DistributedSampler (seed=args.seed, drop_last) gives rank r positions r + world*j of one global permutation, so update u consumes exactly captions [16u, 16u+16) in both 2x8 and 4x4, with the same mean-of-16 gradient; epochs = 16 in both; LSF STEPS = 3000 in both. What does differ: the Delta draws per caption visit come from a per-rank RNG stream (delta_rng, lines 607/1072), the ranking rollout noise is keyed by (rank, micro) (rank_utils.py:165), rank-0-only side computations see different captions (reward refresh rbuf line 1274/1490, monitors), bf16 reduction order, and GPU type (B1/A s0 and controls on H100, A/B2 s1-s2 on H200). Runs affected: B2 s0 151399 (2x8) vs A/B1/naive/ours s0 (4x4); naive 151349/151357 and ours 151361/151403 (2x8) vs A/B2 s1-s2 (4x4).
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:746-749 (sampler), 607 and 1072 (delta_rng per rank), 1274 and 1490 (rbuf on rank 0); args.json accum field: 8 for 151349/151357/151361/151399, 4 elsewhere; bjobs placement in this review.
findings.consequence: Comparisons involving those runs are unpaired in the Delta stream; since seed pairing shows ~zero correlation anyway (F3) the power loss is small, but the analysis must not claim pairing, and B2's three seeds are heterogeneous in world size.
findings.fix: Analyze as independent runs; record world size per run in the results table; keep world size constant within a seed index for any additional seeds.

findings.title: Held-out probe: latent columns are not leak-free, and its pair statistics have no clustered uncertainty
findings.detail: probe_heldout.py excludes only the 3k pool by prompt and reference (lines 75-77). The projector P was pretrained on ~22k captions of the same 118k cache (train split; the replay set is 2k of them), so roughly 19% of the 300 probe captions (~57) are expected to be P training captions: the 'latent' and 'latent_g' columns are optimistic relative to unseen captions (rgb columns, the student and the head are unaffected). Statistically, 833 pairs are clustered in 300 captions (binomial SE ~0.017 unclustered, ~0.025 clustered); per-family n is 27 (3d_spatial), 79 (shape), 81 (texture). The reported base 0.565 -> naive 0.606 -> ours 0.627 rgb accuracies and the per-family pattern are therefore within 1-2 SE of each other.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/probe_heldout.py:59-61,75-87; /lustre/.../phaseW/latent_scorer/build_pooled_artifacts.py:51-53,97 (replay from split=train; P trained on the non-3k splits); /lustre/.../phaseW/rank/probe/{base,hp1_naive_s0,hp1_ours_s0}.json summaries (n_pairs 833; 3d_spatial 27).
findings.consequence: The probe is the cheapest decisive measurement in the campaign, but as run it cannot separate arms by less than ~0.03-0.05 accuracy and its latent-space numbers carry a mild optimistic bias.
findings.fix: Exclude P's train/val idx (D['split'] in the pooled artifact) from the probe pool; report caption-clustered bootstrap CIs and a McNemar/paired test across models on identical (caption, negative, noise) pairs; raise n to >=1000 captions (single GPU, ~30-60 min); run it on the saved rank_head_step*.pt of every arm so head generalization is tracked over training.

findings.title: Under cosine-to-zero the averaged checkpoint equals the raw final one; the '-avg' eval duplicates ~1.5 GPU-h per run
findings.detail: naive avg vs raw: mean +0.0014, per-prompt SD 0.087; ours avg vs raw: -0.0001, SD 0.073 (vs 0.155 between arms). The last three checkpoints are near-identical because the LR is already ~0.
findings.evidence: Computed from /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseN/eval_W_B2-hp1_3k-hp1{,-avg}_s0_1452{50,51} and eval_W_CD_dinop_hard-rewRi-s16-hp1_3k-hp1{,-avg}_s0_1452{52,53}.
findings.consequence: Twelve of the pending eval jobs in rank_jobs.txt/hp1_jobs.txt buy almost no information; that budget would fund 2-3 extra seeds' evals.
findings.fix: Keep one eval per run (the averaged one, for continuity with the references) and redirect the saved GPU-h to seeds 3-4 of the primary contrast.

findings.title: g is trained on 4-step rollout terminals but applied (B1, A) to Tweedie x0_hat estimates from teacher states; no check that the shaped geometry transfers
findings.detail: The ranking loss shapes g on P(z_K) of the student's w=1 rollouts (train line 1393-1400); the shaped reward is applied to P(x0_hat) at the two least-noisy supervised states of the teacher trajectory (lines 1245-1256). These are different input distributions to P (rollout endpoints vs one-step clean estimates from sigma ~0.1-0.3), and P itself is refreshed on x0_hat only.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1245-1256 and 1389-1400; the probe outputs show P-space accuracy is already near chance on rollouts (latent 0.537 vs rgb 0.606 for naive).
findings.consequence: B1/A could show no effect simply because g's ordering does not hold on x0_hat, which the current logs cannot distinguish from 'prompt-aware geometry does not help'.
findings.fix: Cheap diagnostic: for captions with negatives, run one extra no-grad student forward at the k7 state with each negative's embedding, take the Tweedie x0_hat, and log the pairwise accuracy of <g(P(.)), g(u_ref)> on x0_hat (raw and shaped). If it sits at chance, the transfer path is broken before the benchmark is consulted.

findings.title: A's only gradient beyond B1 is 'push negative-prompt generations away from the photo'; degrade-the-loser is unmonitored
findings.detail: With the softmax partial order the positive receives (1-p_pos)/kappa of the push and the negatives -p_j/kappa; in A the negatives' rollouts carry gradient into the student, so half the ranking pressure can be satisfied by worsening generations of legitimate prompts ('Three friends ...', 'yellow tour bus'), which are exactly the CompBench prompt types. With the negatives detached, A collapses to a softmax-weighted reward, i.e. B1. This project has already seen a preference loss take its margin from the loser.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:85-88; /lustre/.../phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1405-1416; 151316 log: acc_shaped 0.85-0.89 and loss 0.57 by steps 1150-1300 with no per-side raw score logged (r_pos is the shaped positive only).
findings.consequence: A could improve its own ranking metric and the benchmark could stay flat or fall on the negatives' families; the current logging cannot attribute the margin to the winner or the loser.
findings.fix: Log mean raw projector score of positives and of negatives separately (R_raw[0] and R_raw[1:]) and their true-DINO counterparts in the monitor; run the held-out probe on A's existing checkpoint_step1000/1500 + rank_head (if latent_g accuracy far exceeds rgb_g on A's own rollouts it is hacking P; if negatives' rgb positive_score falls it is degrading losers); add a control arm with the negatives' embeddings detached.

findings.title: The kappa -> infinity sanity arm is redundant with 'ours' by construction; the informative controls are shuffled negatives and a share-matched reward
findings.detail: With fc2 zero-initialised and a flat softmax the head's gradient is zero; AdamW weight decay keeps fc2 at zero, so g stays the identity and lambda_rank=0 gives ours exactly. A shuffled-negatives arm (negatives borrowed from other captions, same rollout compute) tests whether the structured text order matters at all; F1's share-matched ours tests whether the reward strength is the driver.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:27-36 (zero-init fc2); train line 890 (AdamW wd 0.01).
findings.consequence: Compute spent on kappa -> inf would reproduce ours; without a shuffled-negatives control a positive B1/A result cannot be attributed to the ranking content.
findings.fix: Skip kappa -> inf; add shuffled negatives (one seed each for B1 and A) and the share-matched ours (F1).

findings.title: Head and align optimizers run at constant lr 1e-4 while the student's cosine LR decays to 0
findings.detail: rank_head_opt/align_opt have no schedule (lines 890, 897, 1460-1464). In B1 the reward target keeps moving at full speed after the student can no longer follow, and the saved rank_head_final is not co-converged with the student; the observed 'shaped reward drifts down while raw rises' is partly this.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:890,897,1455-1464.
findings.consequence: Small for the student (its LR is ~0 late), but the final head used by the probe reflects the last few hundred updates of a moving target rather than the geometry the student was trained against.
findings.fix: Tie the head/align LR to the student's multiplier, or freeze g over the last 20% of updates; probe both rank_head_step2000 and rank_head_final.

findings.title: B2's alignment acts at a single near-clean state (last rollout step, sigma 0.009 -> 0) and its loss saturates by step 500
findings.detail: grad_last=True keeps the graph only through the final rollout forward, so the DiT block-8 features are aligned at one input state that is never a supervised consistency state (k4..k7 of the 8-step teacher schedule). The target is the student's own generation's shaped embedding, an easy self-consistency target: align loss falls to 0.06-0.16 by step 500 and the remaining gradient share (0.16-0.66) is lambda=60 amplifying a near-zero loss.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:58-82; 151399 log [rank] align 0.245 (step 50) -> 0.064 (step 500); [align-probe] step 500 ratios 0.27/0.38/0.46/0.23/0.66/0.16/0.54/0.51.
findings.consequence: B2 is a weaker test of 'representation transfer' than the note describes (REPA aligns across training timesteps); a null on B2 says little about the transfer idea.
findings.fix: If B2 is kept, align at the supervised states too (hook the CD forward at k6/k7 and target sg[g(P(x0_hat))]), and report the align-loss floor with the result.

findings.title: No pre-registered primary; >=24 implicit tests plus interim wandb reads
findings.detail: 3 arms x 2 references x 2 metrics x {raw, avg} = 24 headline tests, plus 8 categories each, plus the probe's 4 spaces x 7 families; early numbers are already being compared on wandb.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/REVIEW_CONTEXT.md 'Early numbers' section; launchers emit two eval labels per run.
findings.consequence: At alpha 0.05 more than one 'significant' contrast is expected under the null; a post-hoc choice of the best-looking one is not evidence.
findings.fix: Write down now: primary = averaged-checkpoint CompBench mean, arm minus ours, Welch over seeds, Holm across the three arms; everything else descriptive.

findings.title: Verb negatives (17%) and some colour edits are weak O1 negatives; count maps to a noisy category
findings.detail: Sample: 'People walking down a path -> running', 'standing -> sitting', 'big blue sky -> big green sky', 'lush green field -> yellow field'. Verb pairs are often indistinguishable in a still; implausible colour edits may be rendered as the original by the student, giving a pair whose two rollouts are near-identical (uninformative rather than harmful). Families: color 1236, verb 675, count 631, spatial 541, shape 382, texture 286, 3d_spatial 133 (3,884 negatives, 1,816 captions).
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/negatives_3k.json sampled in this review; keying to the cache verified (0 mismatches).
findings.consequence: ~20-25% of pairs carry little ranking signal; per-family conclusions on verb and 3d_spatial (133) will be underpowered.
findings.fix: Weight or drop verb pairs, prefer colour targets plausible for the noun, and use the probe's per-family accuracy of the base model as a filter (families where raw DINO already orders pairs at chance on the base model contribute noise).

findings.title: Two arms are still unbalanced in the queue
findings.detail: B1 s1/s2 (151341, 151345) and ours s1 (151403) are PEND for 4-GPU slots while everything else runs; if they do not start, B1 has one seed and ours two.
findings.consequence: The B1 contrast (the cheapest and cleanest arm) would end single-seed.
findings.fix: Widen placement for those three (2x8 on any 80 GB pair, per the stuck-jobs rule) rather than waiting on the reservation.

validated: args.json diff over the 12 live runs: every training hyperparameter identical (num_steps 3000, warmup 150, lr 1e-5 cosine, window 0.5,0.9 -> score_idxs [4,5,6,7], K 8, N 4, cfg 7, student_cfg 0, huber_c 0, delta 1-3, assign_seed constant, reward lambda 80 / refresh 100 / 16 steps / replay / ref_emb_3k, dino_pool mean) except the intended arm flags (rank_mode, rank_lambda 1.3 only in A, rank_shaped_reward in B1/A, align_lambda 60 only in B2), accum (8 for 151349/151357/151361/151399), and reward_grad_probe_every (0 for 145172/145176 and the naive controls, 500 elsewhere).

target_map_sha256 identical within variant across seeds and world sizes (CD_dinop_hard dbd0d57b... in 145176, 151302, 151316, 151324, 151328, 151332, 151336, 151361, 151399; B2 35d2d955... in 145172, 151349, 151357): all arms train on the same caption->candidate map as the references.

Trainer version: the 09-13 references ran the wandb-snapshotted trainer (wandb/run-20260913_061218-2swko08h/files/code/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py); diffing it against the current file with rank/align lines removed leaves only the probe parameter subset, logging accumulators (_wl_sum etc.), samples_seen accounting, a distance-from-init log, and the inert shaped-reward else-branch, so the non-rank numerics are unchanged.

DistributedSampler equivalence: with seed=args.seed and drop_last, update u consumes the same 16 captions in 2x8 and 4x4 (rank r takes global positions r + world*j), the gradient is the mean of 16 in both, both run 16 epochs, and the LSF STEPS formula gives 3000 for both; n_visits (line 805, ignores accum: 4 vs 2) is only consumed by target_schedule arms and is inert here.

RNG isolation: the head and align inits reseed the global RNG but are wrapped by get/set_rng_state (lines 884-898); rollout noise uses a private generator keyed by (seed, rank, micro) (rank_utils.py:163-166); the ungenerated torch.rand/randn calls at lines 1332/1341/1353 sit in the flow-matching (B5) branch that is not executed; Delta draws use the private delta_rng; rollout_schedule is called once at init and every teacher rollout re-sets K=8 (line 59), so the ranking rollouts do not perturb the consistency branch's timesteps.

Gradient paths: the shaped reward (line 1256) and A's ranking term (1406) use functional_call with detached head params, so nothing in the student's loss trains g; the head's loss (1400-1402) uses detached embeddings, so it never trains the student; B2's alignment target is detached (1421); rank_lambda=0 in B1/B2 keeps _grad_all False so no ranking gradient reaches the student there; head/align grads are all-reduced and averaged, clipped to 1, and stepped identically on every rank after identical seeded init + broadcast.

The reward/rank/align gradient probes are torch.autograd.grad on rank 0 only (no AccumulateGrad hooks, no collectives, no parameter writes), so reward_grad_probe_every 500 vs 0 (ours s0 vs the arms and ours s2) is inert.

Eval chain: EVAL_CFG=1.0 matches the references' alignment.json (cfg 1.0) and student_cfg 0; EVAL_MIN_STEP=3000 is satisfied (145172 checkpoint_final step 3000; checkpoint_avg_last5 carries max step 3000 from 2000/2500/final); STEPS=2000:2500:final maps to files that exist at save_every 500; eval roots include the job id so labels cannot collide; the eval generator seeds per prompt idx (exp0/phaseA_generate.py:137) so prompt-level pairing across models is valid; the hp1 references already passed this exact chain (145250-145253).

negatives_3k.json is keyed by the training cache's idx with matching prompts (0/1816 mismatches), families color 1236 / verb 675 / count 631 / spatial 541 / shape 382 / texture 286 / 3d_spatial 133; sampled edits are same-object rearrangements consistent with the O1 anchor.

Live logs 151302 (B1 s0, step 2750) and 151316 (A s0, step 1300): no errors or warnings beyond a wandb symlink notice; losses, probes and rank metrics finite; memory 74.4 GB; checkpoints and rank_head_step*.pt saved every 500; B1 acc_shaped 0.55-0.74 with acc_raw 0.44-0.70; A acc_shaped rising to 0.85-0.89; the only anomaly is the gradient-share drift reported in F1/F2. The 8-caption RGB monitor is confirmed uninformative (acc_rgb 0.29-0.92 between adjacent readings).
Raw ~ averaged under the cosine schedule confirmed at the prompt level (per-prompt SD 0.07-0.09 within run vs 0.155 between arms; mean difference <= 0.0014).

Held-out probe fairness across models: same 300 captions, same idx-seeded noise, same negatives, g applied to both sides of the cosine exactly as in training; the base/naive/ours ordering (rgb 0.565/0.606/0.627) is internally consistent.
lenses.summary: The experiment as run is faithful in its mechanics: the flags, caption->candidate map, RNG isolation, gradient paths, DDP handling and eval chain all check out, the non-rank trainer numerics are unchanged since the seed-0 references, and I could find no bug in the code paths this campaign exercises. Its problem is that the contrasts are not weight-matched and the statistics are underpowered for the effect size in play. (1) B1's shaped reward runs at 2-3x the realized reward/CD gradient share of ours at matched steps (probe ratios ~0.78 vs ~0.26 at step 1000, rising to 1-3 with strongly negative cosines late), and A's ranking term sits at 0.5-0.9 of the CD gradient instead of the calibrated 0.2 because the 6-update smoke was taken with g at identity and g sharpens 10-40x; so arm-vs-ours conflates prompt-aware geometry with reward strength, which on its own is known to move CompBench by ~0.01. (2) With seed SDs of 0.002-0.010 and no usable seed correlation, n=3 gives an MDE of 0.010-0.026 CompBench and 3-8 GenEval2 points against a few-thousandths target; prompt-level paired tests reach ~0.009 per seed pair (0.005 pooled) but ignore seed variance, and the existing seed-0 pair already shows a Wilcoxon/t disagreement that invites test-shopping. (3) The 2x8/4x4 mix is not a batch-composition confound (same 16 captions per update, verified) but it is a seed-like perturbation of the Delta stream, so the plan should analyze runs as independent. What would make the test decisive: a share-matched ours control (or per-step renormalization of the shaped/ranking gradients) and a shuffled-negatives arm; a pre-registered single primary contrast with 5-8 seeds funded by dropping the redundant raw-checkpoint evals; and the held-out ranking probe, made leak-free (exclude P's training captions), clustered by caption and scaled to >=1000 captions, run on every saved rank_head and on A's existing step-1000/1500 checkpoints to see whether A is improving positives, degrading negatives, or hacking P. If the probe shows the trained head generalizes and the share-matched control does not reproduce B1's result, the path is sound; if the head's held-out accuracy stays near identity, the benchmark runs cannot answer the question regardless of seeds.

findings.title: Held-out probe leaks the projector's pretraining captions and the replay set
findings.detail: probe_heldout.py excludes only the 3k pool (lines 75-77: seen_p/seen_r from --exclude phaseN/coco_selection_dinopatch). The projector P was pretrained on 24,000 captions of the same 118k cache (make_manifests.py lines 22-33: 22k train / 2k val, split recorded in phaseW/latent_scorer/manifest.jsonl), and the replay set used at every refresh is 2,000 of those train captions. Matching the probe's idx against manifest.jsonl: 61 of the 300 probe captions are P's TRAIN captions and 9 its VAL captions (70/300 = 23%, same caption AND same photo, since the 118k cache has exactly one caption per photo); matching replay_2k.pt's e_ref against ref_emb_118k.pt (best cosine >= 0.99986 for all 2,000) shows 9 probe captions are also in the replay set, i.e. their teacher candidates and photo embeddings are re-fit into P every 100 updates of every 'ours'/rank run. Empirically the identity-head numbers are not inflated by it (latent acc on the seen subset vs unseen: naive 0.539/0.537, ours 0.529/0.539, B1 latent_g 0.560/0.592), but the rgb accuracies of all three students are ~0.05 higher on the seen subset (0.644/0.681/0.649 vs 0.595/0.611/0.601, n=191 vs 642), so the subset is not exchangeable with the rest.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/probe_heldout.py:75-77; /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/latent_scorer/make_manifests.py:22-33; computed overlap: probe idx in manifest split -> {train: 61, val: 9}; probe idx in replay set -> 9; e.g. all 70 also match by prompt text and by reference path.
findings.consequence: 'latent' / 'latent_g' accuracies are partly measured on data P was fit on; once the trained heads are probed the claim 'the shaped space generalises to unseen captions' is contaminated for 23% of pairs, and any P-fidelity comparison (latent vs rgb) is optimistic on that subset. It also breaks the README's 'caption and photo both unseen' statement.
findings.fix: Add a manifest exclusion: load phaseW/latent_scorer/manifest.jsonl and drop every idx/prompt/reference with split in {train, val} (86,948 clean held-out captions remain, ~32.6k of them with >= 2 negatives, so N is not a constraint). Re-run the three existing probes (113 s of GPU each per the logs) so all rows share the clean draw.

findings.title: The probe evaluates the head in the PRETRAINED projector's space, but the head was trained on the REFRESHED projector, which is never saved
findings.detail: The trainer refreshes P every 100 updates for 16 steps on decoded recent predictions plus replay (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1505-1528) and the ranking head g is trained on that live P's outputs (line 1396 `_e = proj(_zK)`, line 1400 head loss on `_e.detach()`). The checkpoint writers at lines 1661-1686 save the student, `rank_head` (+ `align_proj`) and the EMA model only; `proj.state_dict()` is never written. probe_heldout.py loads `--proj phaseW/latent_scorer/projector/projector.pt` (line 56, 102-104), i.e. the pretrained P. So the probe's `latent` and `latent_g` rows for a trained run apply g to a space it was not fit to; the docstring's claim that `latent_g` is 'what the ranking loss optimised' (line 16) is false for every rank arm.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1396,1400,1505-1528,1661-1686 (no proj save); /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/probe_heldout.py:56,102-104; B1_s0_final.json: latent_g 0.585 vs in-training rank/acc_shaped 0.65 (REVIEW_CONTEXT line 73) — the gap conflates held-out generalisation with the P mismatch.

findings.fix: Save {'model': proj.state_dict()} next to rank_head_*.pt (~40 MB; the trainer already keeps proj on rank 0), add PROJ to probe.lsf and pass it as --proj. Until then, report only rgb / rgb_g for trained heads and label latent/latent_g as 'pretrained P'.

findings.title: The latent projector carries almost no prompt-edit information, so the head is being trained on a near-chance signal
findings.detail: Across the three identity-head probes the projector space orders the positive above a negative at 0.499 (base), 0.538 (naive), 0.537 (ours) — chance to +0.04 — while true DINO on the same decoded rollouts gives 0.565 / 0.606 / 0.627. Per pair, the rgb and latent margins correlate at Pearson 0.24-0.33 (Spearman 0.22-0.26), sign agreement 0.57, and within-caption Spearman over the m prompts is 0.14-0.17. That is expected: P was trained to preserve the ranking over 4 NOISE candidates of the SAME prompt (train_projector.py:150-151, KL over candidates; refresh line 1521 idem), never over prompt edits, and it is out of distribution on 4-step w=1 rollouts (positive cosine to u_ref 0.41 in P vs 0.61 in rgb). The first trained-head probe confirms the consequence: B1 latent_g 0.585 (up from 0.533) but rgb_g 0.607 vs rgb 0.612 — the head does not improve the true-feature ordering at all (B1 vs ours rgb_g: 114/130 discordant, p=0.34), and B1's own generations rank worse in rgb than ours (0.612 vs 0.627, n.s.).
findings.evidence: probe JSONs: per-pair margin correlation rgb vs latent (base +0.327, naive +0.242, ours +0.235), sign agreement 0.576/0.569/0.569; /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/latent_scorer/train_projector.py:150-151; /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1521; B1_s0_final.json summary rgb 0.612 / latent 0.533 / latent_g 0.585 / rgb_g 0.607.
findings.consequence: The implementation's ranking loss shapes g on P(z_K), whose ordering of positive vs negative is ~55/45 at best; whatever g learns is a reweighting of noise plus the small prompt component, and rgb_g shows none of it reaches true DINO features. This is the most likely reason a B1/B2/A CompBench effect would be null, and it is not a test of the design note's hypothesis (which is stated on f(x0_hat) = DINO of pixels).
findings.fix: Train and probe g on true DINO features of the decoded rollouts (the probe already decodes; decode is ~61 ms/image per the measured cost, so m<=4 decodes add ~0.25 s to B1's 4.0 s/update). Add a P-fidelity metric to the probe: within-caption Spearman(P, rgb) over the m prompts and the sign agreement of margins, reported per family — it should exceed ~0.5 before P is used as the ranking input.

findings.title: The 'base' probe row is a floor, not a premise test: SD3.5-M sampled at 4 Euler steps, guidance 1
findings.detail: probe.lsf runs `--ckpt base` with STEPS=4 and the probe's student_rollout has no CFG path (one conditional pass, rank_utils.py:76-80). The undistilled base at 4 unguided steps produces near-garbage: its positive rgb score is 0.360 vs 0.607-0.612 for the students. Its pairwise accuracy (rgb 0.565, latent 0.499) therefore says nothing about whether raw DINO orders the positive first on realistic images (the design note's premise) nor where the teacher sits.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/probe.lsf:29 (STEPS default 4); /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:58-82; base.json summary positive_score rgb 0.360 (naive 0.607, ours 0.612).
findings.consequence: The 'base 0.565 -> student 0.606-0.627' progression cannot be read as 'distillation makes DINO more prompt-aware'; the comparison is confounded by image quality. The premise test and the teacher reference are missing.
findings.fix: Add a CFG path to the probe (neg_emb + cfg as in phaseW/latent_scorer/gen_latents.py rollout, lines 25-40) and run the teacher at 8 steps w=7 (the training-time teacher) and the base at 28 steps w=7 as the two reference rows; ~2-6 min each for 300 captions.

findings.title: 833 pairs on 300 captions cannot resolve the effects being chased; every naive-vs-ours and per-family contrast is non-significant
findings.detail: Binomial SE at n=833 is 0.017; the caption-clustered SE (300 captions, ~2.8 correlated pairs each) is 0.021. Paired on identical captions and noise: rgb naive 0.606 vs ours 0.627, discordant 114/97, McNemar p=0.27 (the margin difference is +0.004, Wilcoxon p=0.025, caption-level paired t p=0.031); latent 0.538 vs 0.537, 114/115, p=1.0; base vs naive rgb 198/164, p=0.083. Per family n=27 (3d_spatial) to 293 (colour), SE 0.03-0.10; all seven per-family deltas are n.s. (colour +0.031 p=0.33, spatial +0.052 p=0.47, verb +0.048 p=0.36, count -0.015, texture -0.037, 3d_spatial +0.074 on 4/2 discordant). With ~25% discordant pairs, SE(diff) = 0.5/sqrt(n): the MDE at 80% power is 0.048 for 833 pairs; detecting 0.03 needs ~2,200 pairs (~800 captions), 0.02 needs ~4,900 pairs (~1,800 captions).
findings.evidence: Computed from phaseW/rank/probe/{hp1_naive_s0,hp1_ours_s0,base}.json (identical idx and negatives lists across files, asserted); probe_heldout.py:141-150 pools pairs without clustering; timing from logs/lsf-sd-W-rank-probe-151429.out: 300 captions in ~113 s on one GPU.
findings.consequence: The per-family table in REVIEW_CONTEXT (lines 83-84) is noise at this N, and the headline 'ours 0.627 > naive 0.606' is not established at p<0.05 on accuracy. A B1/B2/A vs ours difference of the size seen (B1 rgb -0.014) is undetectable.
findings.fix: Raise --n to 1,500-2,000 clean captions (~10-13 min per model), add --noise_seeds 2-4 per caption to average the shared-noise draw, compute accuracy per caption then a caption-level bootstrap CI, and report McNemar/sign p per family plus a family macro-average. Store per-pair records (already done) so future arms are compared paired.

findings.title: The B1 probe used the raw final checkpoint while the naive/ours references used the 3-checkpoint average
findings.detail: logs/lsf-sd-W-rank-probe-151529.out and B1_s0_final.json: ckpt = .../rankB1-hp1-acc4_s0_151302/checkpoint_final.pt (step 3000); the references (151429/151430) loaded checkpoint_avg_last5.pt (average of 2000/2500/final, average_ckpts.lsf via launch_rank.sh:44). Per-checkpoint weight noise is +-0.02 on CompBench, the same order as the differences being read (B1 rgb 0.612 vs ours 0.627).
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/probe/B1_s0_final.json ckpt field; /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/probe/hp1_ours_s0.json ckpt field; /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/launch_rank.sh:44-45.

findings.fix: Probe the averaged student (checkpoint_avg_last5.pt, produced by the chain's AV job) with rank_head_final.pt (the head has no averaging; it is the final head in every case), and label files by checkpoint type.

findings.title: The reward and the ranking head operate on different inputs of P: one-step x0_hat predictions vs 4-step rollouts
findings.detail: The anchor reward (B1's shaped reward included) is computed on P(x0_hat) of the two least-noisy supervised states (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1245-1258), while g is trained on P(z_K) of full 4-step w=1 rollouts (lines 1389-1400) and the probe scores 4-step rollouts. P's positive cosine on rollouts is 0.41 (probe) vs ~0.45 on x0_hat (reward/proj_score in the audit), and P is refreshed only on x0_hat + teacher replay, never on rollouts. So B1 applies a head fit on rollout embeddings to x0_hat embeddings, and the probe's `latent` row is not the reward's operating point.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1245-1258 (reward on x_hat[_order]), 1389-1400 (rank on rollouts), 1505-1528 (refresh on rbuf x0_hat + replay); REVIEW_CONTEXT lines 75-76 (shaped reward drifts down while raw rises).
findings.consequence: The observed B1 behaviour (shaped reward 0.43 -> 0.34 while the raw projector score rises) is consistent with g reshaping a rollout-space that the reward states never visit; the 'transfer' path in B1 is not the one the head was trained for.
findings.fix: Either compute the shaped reward on rollout embeddings too (one extra rollout is already paid in the rank block), or add the reward states' x0_hat to the head's training set; in the probe, add a `latent_x0hat` row (P of the one-step prediction from the K=6/7 states of the same z0 chain) so the reward space is probed directly.

findings.title: Per-family accuracies ignore clustering and the family mix is dominated by colour; 3d_spatial has 27 pairs
findings.detail: Each caption contributes up to 3 pairs of the same or different families (233 captions with 3 negatives, 67 with 2), and the 'all' accuracy weights families by their frequency: colour 293/833 (35%), count 132, verb 124, spatial 97, texture 81, shape 79, 3d_spatial 27. The summary (probe_heldout.py:141-150) pools pairs, so the 3d_spatial row (SE ~0.10) is uninformative and the 'all' row mostly measures colour edits. The >= 2 negatives filter also selects attribute-rich captions (in a 5k clean sample 39% of captions have 0 negatives, 23% have 1).
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseW/rank/probe_heldout.py:141-150; family pair counts computed from hp1_naive_s0.json; clean-pool negatives distribution computed with negatives_for over 5,000 held-out captions: {0: 1971, 1: 1154, 2: 356, 3: 1519}.
findings.consequence: Family-level conclusions (e.g. 'texture 0.74, verb 0.70') carry +-0.05-0.10 error bars and the 'all' number cannot be compared across probes with different family mixes.
findings.fix: Report per-family accuracy with caption-clustered bootstrap CIs, a macro-average over families, and cap pairs per family per caption at 1 when computing the headline; consider sampling the probe stratified by family (the clean pool has ~32k captions with >= 2 negatives, so 300+ per family is available for every family but 3d_spatial).

findings.title: Three seeds on CompBench cannot resolve the size of effect at stake; state the MDE and use per-prompt rows + more images per prompt
findings.detail: A seed-paired t-test with n=3 has df=2 (t_crit 4.30); MDE at 80% power is ~3.1 x sd of the seed-paired difference. The converged-schedule ours-naive gap is +0.0017 (0.4860 vs 0.4877); the constant-LR 3-seed result (+0.0149, p=0.004) implies a seed-paired sd of ~0.002 on averaged models, which would give an MDE of ~0.006, but the documented +-0.02 per-checkpoint swing means sd_d can be 0.005-0.01 for raw finals (MDE 0.015-0.03). The eval generates ONE image per prompt (phaseA_generate.py --n_seeds default 1, seed = --seed + idx shared across models), 2,398 CompBench prompts (val split, 300/category, spatial 298) and 800 GenEval2 prompts; per-prompt scores are saved (compbench_eval.py:367 'per_prompt', geneval2_eval.py:173), so prompt-level paired Wilcoxon/t are available and are the higher-powered test at fixed weights.
findings.evidence: /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/exp0/phaseA_generate.py:48-53,137; /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/phaseC/compbench_eval.py:354-368; /lustre/scratch126/cellgen/lotfollahi/ha11/EnergyVLM/ablations/phaseN_eval_alignment.lsf:80-83; REVIEW_CONTEXT lines 21-22, 102-104.
findings.consequence: A null result for B1/B2/A vs ours at 3 seeds is uninformative unless the MDE is reported; a positive result must survive both the seed-paired test (weights as random) and the prompt-paired test (prompts as random).
findings.fix: Always evaluate the averaged checkpoint; pass --n_seeds 4 to phaseA_generate for the final comparison (4x generation time, scoring unchanged in count of prompts if per-prompt scores are averaged first); report the seed-paired difference with its sd and the implied MDE, and the prompt-level paired test on per_prompt rows restricted to the mapped categories.

findings.title: Metrics the final comparison should report, and how CompBench categories map onto negative families
findings.detail: (1) Generation-level: rgb pairwise accuracy of each student's own rollouts on clean held-out captions (naive / ours / B1 / B2 / A), paired McNemar per family — this is P-free and is the direct test of 'prompt-awareness transferred into the generator'; current values naive 0.606, ours 0.627, B1 0.612. (2) Head transfer: rgb_g - rgb per family (does g re-order true DINO features toward the text order); B1 shows -0.005 overall, verb +0.032, count +0.038, texture -0.062, 3d -0.074. (3) Space-shaping: latent_g - latent with the REFRESHED P (E2). (4) Ordering beyond pairs: Kendall tau is only meaningful with a graded target; obtain one by scoring every negative's generation with VQAScore against the POSITIVE caption (t2v_metrics is vendored) — that also gives a ground truth of contradiction per negative and flags null edits; then report tau between each space's scores and VQAScore over the m prompts, and pooled AUC of margins. (5) Calibration: accuracy in margin deciles and the margin sd — the head inflates the margin sd 0.032 -> 0.090 (latent) and 0.061 -> 0.093 (rgb) without changing accuracy, so accuracy-at-fixed-quantile is the honest view. (6) CompBench mapping for per-category deltas from per_prompt rows: color -> color, numeracy -> count, spatial -> spatial, 3d_spatial -> 3d_spatial, texture -> texture, shape -> shape, non_spatial -> verb (CompBench non-spatial prompts are actions/interactions, the verb family), complex -> unmapped. Present probe per-family deltas and the mapped CompBench per-category deltas side by side with CIs. (7) Cheap nulls inside the probe: score each rollout against a SHUFFLED u_ref (another caption's photo) — accuracy must fall to 0.5 — and against the teacher's 8-step w=7 generation of the positive as a second anchor.
findings.evidence: B1_s0_final.json per-family rows; margin sds computed from hp1_naive_s0/hp1_ours_s0/B1_s0_final; alignment.json per-category keys in phaseN/eval_W_CD_dinop_hard-rewRi-s16-hp1_3k-hp1-avg_s0_145253/alignment.json (3d_spatial, color, complex, non_spatial, numeracy, shape, spatial, texture).
findings.consequence: Without (1)-(3) separated, a CompBench change cannot be attributed to the head vs the reward vs noise; without (6) the per-family probe cannot be cross-checked against the benchmark it is meant to predict.
findings.fix: Extend probe_heldout.py with --noise_seeds, --shuffle_ref, --vqa (t2v_metrics VQAScore of each generation against the positive caption), per-family clustered CIs and a macro average; add a small script that joins per_prompt rows of two evals by prompt text (idx is per-job) and reports paired deltas per mapped category.

findings.title: In-training RGB ranking monitor decodes only the last 8 captions
findings.detail: train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1471 iterates rank_buf[-8:] for rank/acc_rgb and rank/acc_rgb_shaped every 100 updates, giving values of 0.29-0.96 (REVIEW_CONTEXT line 78); the reward monitor next to it uses rbuf[-32:] (line 1490).

validated: 3k-pool exclusion is correct: probe_heldout.py:75-77 excludes by caption text and by reference photo; 0 of the 300 probe captions/photos are in phaseN/coco_selection_dinopatch, and the 118k cache has exactly one caption per photo (113,948 distinct references), so caption-level exclusion equals photo-level exclusion.

Reference embeddings are indexed correctly: ref_emb_118k.pt is a {cache idx -> fp16 unit vector} dict built by build_ref_emb.py with the offline scorer's preprocessing (512x512 bicubic squash, HF processor resize 256 / crop 224, CLS dropped, patch mean, L2-norm); probe_heldout.py:126 indexes it by the same idx, and OnlineScorer.embed (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:102-107) applies identical preprocessing to the decoded rollouts, so the rgb space equals the offline scorer.

The head is applied consistently: the probe applies g to both the generation embedding and u_ref (probe_heldout.py:133) exactly as the trainer does (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1400, 1256), loads the 'head' key the trainer saves (lines 1666, 1680), and an absent head is the identity (RankHead's zero-init last layer), so latent == latent_g and rgb == rgb_g in the identity probes (verified to 1e-6).

Eval chain settings for the 3k runs are right: launch_rank.sh:43-45 and launch_hp1.sh:31-33 pass EVAL_CFG=1.0 (guidance-distilled students; the LSF's default 7.0 would be wrong for these) and EVAL_MIN_STEP=3000 (the LSF's default 6000 would reject every 3k checkpoint); average_checkpoints.py:45 stamps the averaged file with the max member step so the step guard passes; the ledgers show train -> eval-final, train -> average -> eval-avg dependencies for every arm.

The alignment eval is what it claims: phaseN_eval_alignment.lsf generates at 4 steps, 1 image per prompt with seed = --seed + idx shared across models (phaseA_generate.py:137), 2,398 CompBench val-split prompts (300 per category, spatial 298) and 800 GenEval2 prompts; compbench collect uses --routing_split val, matching the pool's split=val (pool manifest configuration); per-prompt rows are saved (compbench_eval.py:367, geneval2_eval.py:173) so prompt-level paired tests are feasible; the pool manifest hashes are re-verified before generation.

The replay set is drawn from the projector's train split only (all 2,000 replay e_ref vectors match ref_emb_118k entries whose manifest split is 'train'), so the replay never touches the 3k pool; the projector's test split is exactly the 3k pool (manifest.jsonl: 22,000 train / 2,000 val / 3,000 test), consistent with the README's claim that P never saw the training captions.
lenses.summary: The evaluation machinery is mostly sound (3k exclusion, pairing by idx-seeded noise, DINO preprocessing, eval CFG/min-step, averaged checkpoints, per-prompt rows) but the held-out probe has three problems that undermine what it can conclude. (1) It leaks: 70/300 probe captions (23%) are the projector's own train/val captions and 9 are in the replay set that P is re-fit on every 100 updates; a clean pool of 86,948 captions exists, so the fix is one filter. (2) The trainer never saves the refreshed projector, so the probe's latent/latent_g rows for trained heads apply g to the pretrained P, not the space g was trained on. (3) Most importantly, the projector space itself is near chance at ordering positive vs edited prompts (0.50-0.54 vs 0.57-0.63 for true DINO; per-pair margin correlation 0.24-0.33, sign agreement 0.57), and the first trained-head probe shows the head raises latent_g to 0.585 while rgb_g equals rgb (0.607 vs 0.612) — the shaping never reaches true features. Statistically, 833 pairs give an MDE of ~0.05 on paired accuracy; naive vs ours rgb (+0.020, McNemar p=0.27) and every per-family delta are non-significant, and the B1 probe compared a raw final checkpoint against averaged references. The base row (4 steps, w=1, positive score 0.36) is a floor, not a premise test. Recommended: filter the manifest, save P, probe on 1,500-2,000 clean captions with 2-4 noises and clustered CIs, add teacher/base-CFG reference rows, a shuffled-reference null and VQAScore-graded negatives, train/probe the head on true DINO features, and cross-check per-family probe deltas against per-category CompBench deltas (color->color, numeracy->count, spatial->spatial, 3d_spatial->3d_spatial, texture->texture, shape->shape, non_spatial->verb) from per_prompt rows with the seed-paired MDE stated.

Read-only review of phaseW/rank (B1/B2/A on top of "ours"). Code: the gradient paths, RNG isolation, DDP handling, scheduler restore, checkpoint/hook interplay and the probe's held-out selection are correct (validated list below). The problems are in what the arms can actually test. (1) Both B arms train the head g on the latent projector's space, where the held-out pos>neg signal is at chance (probe latent 0.499/0.538/0.537 vs true DINO 0.565/0.606/0.627), so the 0.65-0.74 training accuracy must be caption memorisation or a rule-vocabulary shortcut; the trained heads have not been probed held-out, and when they are, the probe will apply g on the PRE-TRAINED projector while g was fit on the refreshed one (never saved). (2) The trainable head silently re-scales the shaped reward: the reward-gradient share tuned to ~0.3 at step 0 rises to 0.8-2.9 by steps 1000-2000 in B1 and A with cos(CD,reward) of -0.6 to -0.8 (logs 151302/151316), while B2's raw reward stays at 0.2-0.5; with clip=1 always active this changes B1/A's update direction independently of prompt-awareness. (3) B2's alignment target is g(P(z_K)) of the student's own output, read at sigma=0.009 (the last of the 4-step rollout), so the projector fits it in 250 updates and no ranking information reaches the student; B2 is 'ours + a self-alignment regulariser at sigma~0'. (4) A solves the ranking on training captions by step ~1500 (rank_loss 0.000, margin 0.38, acc 0.95) with an unbounded push-away on the negatives' generations and no monitor of their quality. (5) B1 s0 raw-final CompBench is 0.4868 vs ours-raw 0.4880 (-0.0011 +- 0.0025 per-prompt paired, p=0.65) and naive-raw 0.4848 (+0.0020 +- 0.0032): no effect at seed 0; the same-run avg-vs-raw checkpoint noise on this schedule is only +-0.0015, and ours-vs-naive itself is +0.0017 to +0.0031 (n.s. by t; the Wilcoxon p<0.01 comes from near-zero-variance categories). Negatives: 41% of 3-negative captions have three edits of the same span (near-duplicate images), 14% of targets are weak contradictions ('far from', 'dropping'), the 'shape' family is 86% size antonyms while CompBench shape is geometry, and the spatial family is 87% 'far from'/'under' while CompBench spatial is 71% left/right/top/bottom. DINO's own invariances (colour jitter/grayscale, horizontal flip, patch-mean pooling) cap the colour and left/right signal at chance (probe colour 0.49-0.59, count 0.57), so no head can recover it. Verdict: the O1 anchor logic is sound where DINO already carries a signal (texture 0.74-0.78, verb 0.65-0.70), but as implemented the campaign cannot separate 'head learned composition' from 'head memorised/shortcut' nor 'student improved' from 'reward moved'. Decisive next steps, cheapest first: an offline head study on cached rollouts (P vs true-DINO features, shuffled labels, anchor-swap null, family-held-out) plus the trained-head/A-student held-out probes with n>=1000 and a VQAScore ceiling on the negatives (all <1 GPU-h); then, only if the head shows held-out signal, frozen-head B1 with a reward-scale guard, B2 aligned at a noisy state to g(u_ref), and COCO-annotation-verified count/spatial negatives. Falsifier: trained-head held-out rgb_g/latent_g <= raw + 0.02 (or equal to the anchor-swap null), and B1/A/B2 <= ours + 0.01 on the family-matched CompBench categories over 3 seeds.
validated: Gradient paths are as claimed: the head's loss uses _e.detach() (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1400-1402) so only g trains; Variant A's ranking term and the shaped reward use head_apply(..., False), which substitutes detached parameters via torch.func.functional_call (rank_utils.py:39-45), so the student's gradient reaches P and the rollout chain but never g (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1256, 1406); B2's target is g(P(z_K)).detach() (line 1421) and the hook's feature path carries grad to student blocks 1-8 and align.proj.

DDP handling: rollouts run on every rank on every micro-step (rank_every=1), captions without negatives roll out the positive alone with a zero loss so forward counts match (lines 1391-1394, 1401, 1407); head and align.proj gradients are all-reduced and averaged then clipped before their optimizer steps (lines 1460-1464); identical init via torch.manual_seed(seed+424242)+broadcast (887-889, 893-896). Multiple DDP forwards before one backward are legal with find_unused_parameters=False (AccumulateGrad fires once per param); runs are alive past step 1500 with 74.4 GB.

RNG isolation: rollout noise comes from a private generator keyed by (seed, rank, micro) (rank_utils.py:163-166); the head/align inits save and restore the global CPU+CUDA RNG (lines 884, 898); target_map_sha256 is identical (dbd0d57b...) in 151302, 151316, 151399, 151328 and the control 145176, so caption order and candidate selection are matched across all arms at the same seed.

Scheduler state: rollout_schedule sets 4 steps then restores K=8 (rank_utils.py:48-55) and rollout_states re-sets K on every call (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:59), so the CD branch always reads the 8-step schedule; the rollout sigmas [1.0, 0.858, 0.602, 0.009, 0.0] are the pipeline's own 4-step schedule that the eval also uses.

Checkpoint/hook interplay in B2: rank_head_step*.pt saves head + align_proj + rank args (lines 1666-1668, 1680-1682); the AlignHook only stores while armed so log_student_samples and checkpoint saves are unaffected; features() refuses a no-grad capture (rank_utils.py:134-135) and diffusers 0.32.2 uses non-reentrant checkpointing, so the captured block-8 output is differentiable (confirmed by the runs not raising).

Reference embeddings: ref_emb_3k.pt and ref_emb_118k.pt are dicts keyed by caption idx (3000 and 113948 entries), so ref_emb[int(idx)] in the trainer (line 1247, 1397) and the probe (probe_heldout.py:126) is a correct join; all 3000 pool captions appear in the 118k cache with identical prompt and reference; the 118k cache has exactly one caption per photo, so excluding by reference path is exact.

Probe held-out selection: excludes the 3k pool by prompt and by photo, uses the same negatives_for() rules and m=3, seeds the shared noise by caption idx so the three probe runs score identical idx sets (verified) and can be compared paired; identity head gives rgb_g == rgb and latent_g == latent exactly (base 0.565/0.499), as it should.

Run arguments: every rank arm shares the control's hyperparameters (cosine, lr 1e-5, warm-up 150, window 0.5,0.9 -> K={4..7}, accum 4, refresh 100/16, lambda 80) and differs only in rank_*/align_* flags and reward_grad_probe_every=500 (a rank-0 autograd.grad diagnostic that does not touch the update); the smoke-based lambda calibration reproduces at step 0 (rank ratio at w=1 0.09-0.46 -> x1.3; align 0.0036-0.005 -> x60 = 0.13-0.33; reward 0.25-0.33).

The claimed B2 alignment saturation is real: align_loss 0.98 -> 0.245 at step 50 -> 0.08 by 250 -> 0.05-0.07 thereafter (151399, 151328); the claimed shaped-space training accuracy is real: B1 acc_shaped 0.55 -> 0.74 by step 2000 with acc_raw flat at 0.50-0.60 (151302).

CompBench eval chain: per-prompt scores are stored (per_prompt list, 300 per category, 2398 total), so prompt-paired tests are possible; average_checkpoints.py averages student checkpoints only (the head is not averaged, which is correct); checkpoint noise on the converged schedule is small: ours avg-vs-raw -0.0001 +- 0.0015, naive +0.0014 +- 0.0018, so the +-0.02 figure from the constant-LR schedule no longer applies.

Negatives builder: nouns are preserved in every edit (same-object rearrangements as the O1 condition requires), article agreement and plural handling are correct in the 30 sampled captions, and no paraphrase/noun/nonsense edits of the audited kind appeared in the sample.

findings.title: The head is trained on the projector space, where the held-out pos>neg signal is at chance; its 0.65-0.74 training accuracy is unexplained without a held-out probe
findings.detail: Both B arms and A fit g on P(z_K) (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1396-1400). The probe shows P-space pairwise accuracy of 0.499 (base), 0.538 (naive), 0.537 (ours) on 300 unseen captions, with per-family values at or below chance (count 0.42-0.48, spatial 0.46 for the students, colour 0.48-0.56), while true DINO on the same rollouts is 0.565/0.606/0.627. The head sees only the 768-d embedding and u_ref, never the prompt, so on a channel whose ordering information is nil on unseen captions it can only reach 0.65-0.74 on the 1,816 training captions (each visited 16 times) by memorising caption-specific directions or by learning that images with rule-vocabulary content (red/brown/blue, three/four/five, 'far from') are negatives. The latter shortcut transfers to the held-out probe because the probe uses the same rules.
findings.evidence: phaseW/rank/probe/{base,hp1_naive_s0,hp1_ours_s0}.json summaries (latent 0.499/0.538/0.537; rgb 0.565/0.606/0.627); logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151302.out '[rank] step 2000 acc_shaped=0.742 acc_raw=0.555'; negatives_3k.json target vocabulary (red 224, brown 212, blue 193; three 235, four 203, five 127; 'far from' 358 of 541 spatial).
findings.consequence: Any shaped-space accuracy gain can be memorisation or a vocabulary prior rather than prompt-awareness; nothing in the current plan distinguishes them.
findings.fix: P0, <1 GPU-h total: (a) run probe_heldout.py with --head for B1/A/B2 rank_head_final.pt (10 min each) and report latent_g, rgb_g per family; (b) anchor-swap null: re-run the probe saving e_lat/e_rgb per generation and score each caption's pos/neg against a permuted caption's u_ref; if the trained head still orders pos>neg at the same rate it learned an anchor-independent content prior; (c) offline head study on cached rollouts of the ours student (1,816 captions x 4 prompts x 2 noises, ~15 min on 1 GPU): train heads on P vs true-DINO features, with true vs shuffled positives, and family-held-out (train on 6 families, test on the 7th), then probe held-out. This answers 'can any head learn composition from these features' without touching the student.

findings.title: The refreshed projector is never saved, so the planned probe of the trained heads applies g to the wrong P
findings.detail: P is refreshed every 100 updates for 16 steps (lines 1505-1528; 30 refreshes per run) and broadcast, but only rank_head_*.pt (head, align_proj) and checkpoint_*.pt (student) are written (lines 1663-1668, 1677-1682); no proj.state_dict() is saved anywhere (grep confirms). The head g was fit on P_t(z_K) with the drifting projector, while probe_heldout.py loads phaseW/latent_scorer/projector/projector.pt (line 56, 104), i.e. P_0.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'proj.state_dict' phaseW/train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py returns nothing; probe_heldout.py:56 default --proj is the pretrained file; checkpoints/phaseW/phaseW_CD_dinop_hard_3k-rewRi-s16-rankB1-hp1-acc4_s0_151302/ contains only checkpoint_*.pt and rank_head_*.pt.
findings.consequence: A chance-level latent_g for a trained head cannot be attributed to memorisation vs the P mismatch; rgb_g is P-free but g was never trained on DINO's output distribution, so it is a transfer test rather than the quantity the loss optimised.
findings.fix: Save proj.state_dict() next to rank_head_*.pt (10.7M params, trivial) and give the probe a --proj pointing at it; for the three running seeds, the drift can be bounded post hoc by refitting P on the same schedule from the logged refresh losses, but the honest path is to re-probe with the saved P on any re-run. Until then, treat latent_g of trained heads as uninterpretable and rely on rgb_g plus the offline head study of F1.

findings.title: The trainable head inflates the shaped reward's gradient 3-8x and turns it against the CD gradient, so B1 and A no longer run at the calibrated 20-30% reward share
findings.detail: lambda=80 was tuned in the raw space (share 0.25-0.33 at step 0). With g applied to both sides and renormalised, enlarging the pos-neg margin amplifies directions roughly orthogonal to u_ref, which makes cos(g(P(x_hat)), g(u_ref)) far more sensitive to x_hat. The reward-probe lines in B1 show ratio 0.13-0.23 at step 500, 0.60-0.97 at 1000, 0.40-1.93 at 1500 and 0.76-2.28 at 2000, with cos(CD,reward) of -0.70/-0.63 at 1500 and -0.65/-0.81 at 2000; A shows 0.76-1.17 at 1000 and up to 2.90 at 1500. B2, whose reward stays raw, sits at 0.15-0.54 throughout. Because the pre-clip norm is 120-180 and clip=1 is always active, a reward term of comparable norm and negative cosine dominates the direction of every update. The same mechanism explains the shaped reward drifting down (0.43 -> 0.34) while the raw projector score rises: the head shrinks all cosines to widen a margin, and the student chases a target that keeps moving away.
findings.evidence: logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151302.out lines '[reward-probe] step 1500 ... ratio=1.9316 cos(CD,reward)=-0.6959' and 'step 2000 ... ratio=2.2808 cos=-0.6519'; 151316 'step 1500 ... ratio=2.9034'; 151399/151328 reward-probe ratios 0.15-0.55 at 500-1500.
findings.consequence: Any B1/A difference from ours (including B1 s0's -0.001) is confounded with an uncontrolled, growing, anti-distillation reward push that has nothing to do with prompt-awareness; fidelity (not measured in the eval chain) is at risk.
findings.fix: For any re-run: (a) apply g only to the anchor side, r = <P(x_hat), g(u_ref)>, so the student's reward gradient keeps P's scale while g still reweights the space; or (b) hold the share fixed by scaling lambda with a running estimate of ||grad reward||/||grad CD|| from the existing probe (already computed every 500 updates; make it every 50); or (c) bound the head (residual scale 0.1 or spectral norm on fc2). Also log reward/grad_ratio and reward/grad_cos as primary health metrics and add a fidelity number (CMMD/FID on the qual subset) to the eval chain for B1/A.

findings.title: B2's alignment is self-referential and read at sigma=0.009, so it cannot transmit the ranking to the student
findings.detail: The align target is sg[g(P(z_K))] where z_K is the student's own output of the same forward (line 1421), and the hooked forward is the LAST rollout step (grad_last, rank_utils.py:71-79), whose input sigma is 0.009 on the 4-step schedule ([1.0, 0.858, 0.602, 0.009, 0.0]). Block-8 tokens at sigma=0.009 are a deterministic function of an essentially clean latent, and P(z_K) is another function of nearly the same latent, so align.proj (2048-wide MLP, lr 1e-4) simply learns P∘(block-8 embedding)^-1: 0.98 -> 0.08 in 250 updates, then flat. Neither u_ref nor the pos/neg distinction enters the alignment loss; the only 'prompt-aware' content is g's geometry, which per F1 is unverified. REPA's gain comes from aligning NOISY-state features to an EXTERNAL semantic target (the real image); both ingredients are absent.
findings.evidence: train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1419-1422; rank_utils.py:58-82 (grad_last only on k == n-1); logs 151399 '[rank] step 250 ... align=0.0845', 151328 'step 250 align=0.0748'; '[rank] negatives ... rollout sigmas [1.0, 0.858, 0.602, 0.009, 0.0]'.
findings.consequence: B2 is 'ours plus a self-alignment regulariser at sigma~0'; a null result says nothing about representation transfer, and a positive result could not be attributed to prompt-awareness.
findings.fix: If B2 is re-run: align at a noisy rollout step (sigma 0.858 or 0.602; add a grad_step argument) and use an external target: g(u_ref) for the positive prompt's forward (REPA-proper with the real photo), and, to carry the text order without differentiable sampling, a ranking loss on <proj(h_j), g(u_ref)> over the m prompts' noisy-state features. Cost unchanged (~4 s/update, 13 GPU-h per seed). Alternatively drop B2 and spend the budget on F9/F10.

findings.title: Variant A solves the training ranking by step ~1500 with an unbounded push-away on the negatives' generations and no monitor of their quality
findings.detail: By step 1500 the rank-probe reports rank_loss=0.0000, ||grad rank||=0.011-0.021, acc=1.00, and the training window shows acc_shaped 0.954 with margin_shaped +0.38 (raw margin only +0.04, acc_raw 0.77). The loss -log softmax(R/kappa)[0] pushes each negative's rollout away from g(u_ref) with no lower bound except CD on the positive caption; the negatives' prompts are never supervised by CD, so the cheapest solution is to make rule-vocabulary prompts ('a purple bus', 'three men', 'far from') produce images unlike photos. CompBench prompts are exactly that vocabulary. The only in-training image check decodes 8 captions (acc_rgb 0.29-0.96, uninformative) and never scores negatives' images against their own prompts.
findings.evidence: logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151316.out: '[rank-probe] step 1500 ||grad rank||=0.0110 ... rank_loss=0.0000 acc=1.00'; '[rank] step 1550 loss=0.3045 acc_shaped=0.954 acc_raw=0.774 margin_shaped=+0.3825 margin_raw=+0.0411'.
findings.consequence: Half of A's schedule runs with an inactive ranking term (it is B1 plus a saturated head), and a CompBench drop in colour/numeracy for A would be the degenerate solution rather than evidence against the hypothesis; a gain could come from the positive-side push alone (which is the reward, already in ours).
findings.fix: Cheap monitors first (no extra training): every 100 updates decode 32 captions' rollouts and log CLIP/VQAScore of each NEGATIVE generation against its OWN negative prompt and against the positive prompt, plus the positive's true-DINO score. Then: an argmin arm (sign-flipped ranking, 27 GPU-h/seed) only if A shows a gain, to test direction-specificity; a kappa anneal or margin loss to avoid saturation is second-order until F1 shows the ranking generalises.

findings.title: B1 s0 shows no effect, the baseline 'ours' effect has vanished on this schedule, and the pooled Wilcoxon p-values are misleading
findings.detail: Per-prompt paired CompBench (2,398 prompts): B1-raw 0.4868 vs ours-raw 0.4880 = -0.0011 +- 0.0025 (t=-0.46, p=0.65); vs naive-raw +0.0020 +- 0.0032. Ours-vs-naive on the converged schedule is +0.0017 (avg) / +0.0031 (raw), t 0.5-1.0. The Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values (0.003, 0.0006, 0.004) are driven by categories with near-zero variance and tiny consistent shifts (non_spatial +0.0006 +- 0.0007, complex +0.005 +- 0.004), not by compositional categories (spatial -0.027 +- 0.015, numeracy +0.016 +- 0.012). Same-seed per-prompt SE is ~0.003; checkpoint noise (avg vs raw) is ~0.0015; between-seed variance on this schedule is unknown until seeds 1-2 finish, and the 2 GPU x accum 8 controls (151349, 151357, 151361, 151403) and B2 s0 (151399) use a different DistributedSampler split, different micro counters (hence different rollout noise) and different delta_rng streams than the 4x4 arms, so 'seed-paired' comparisons involving them are unpaired in data order.
findings.evidence: Computed from phaseN/eval_W_*_{145250,145251,145252,145253,151303}/compbench_scores/*/scores.json per_prompt lists; train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:607 (delta_rng = seed + rank*1009), 746-751 (sampler by world), rank_utils.py:165 (noise by rank, micro).
findings.consequence: With 3 seeds and an unpaired-in-order control set, the minimal detectable effect on the CompBench mean is roughly 0.01-0.015; B1's true effect at seed 0 is within +-0.005 of ours. A pooled Wilcoxon 'significant' result would be reported for shifts of 0.001 in categories the mechanism cannot touch.
findings.fix: Pre-register the primary endpoint as the family-matched categories (color, texture, 3d_spatial, numeracy) with per-category paired t and a category-clustered test on the pooled mean; report effect sizes with per-prompt SEs; state the MDE once the s1/s2 controls land; do not label 2x8-vs-4x4 contrasts as seed-paired. GenEval2 stays as the evaluator-disjoint check.

findings.title: Negatives: 41% of three-negative captions edit the same span three times, 14% of targets are weak contradictions, and the shape/spatial families do not match CompBench's vocabulary
findings.detail: Of 929 captions with 3 negatives, 380 (40.9%) have all three from the same span (two -> three/four/five; blue -> green/yellow/purple), which are near-duplicate images and give the softmax ~1.5 effective negatives while over-weighting count edits. 536 targets (13.8%) are in a weak-contradiction set ('far from' 358, 'dropping' 121, 'ignoring', 'looking away from', 'resting'): a T2I model largely ignores 'far from', so the generation does not differ and the label is noise for the head. The 'shape' family is 86% size antonyms (large->small 142, small->big 100, little->big 36; only ~30 true shapes) while CompBench shape is geometry (spherical, rectangular, teardrop, pyramidal...). The spatial family is 66% 'next to/near -> far from' and 21% 'on top of -> under', with ~1% left/right, while CompBench spatial is 71% left/right/top/bottom (55/55/52/51 of 298) and 31.8% of those prompts are gated to zero by the evaluator's vocabulary. Count sources are 'two' in 452 of 631 cases; CompBench numeracy uses one (127) as often as four (163). Colour, texture and 3d_spatial map well.
findings.evidence: negatives_3k.json analysis: same-span triplets 380/929; top edits 'next to -> far from' 257, 'standing -> sitting' 223, 'two -> three' 207; phaseFP/eval_pool_101203/compbench_prompts.json relation counts.
findings.consequence: The families with the most negatives (colour 32%, verb 17%, count 16%) are the ones where DINO's signal is weakest or the contradiction is weakest, and the CompBench categories most likely to move (shape, spatial) are not what the negatives train.
findings.fix: CPU-only, P1: cap one negative per span; drop size antonyms and 'far from'/'dropping' targets unless a VQAScore ceiling (F8) shows their generations differ; build count and left/right/top/bottom negatives from COCO instances annotations (boxes and per-category counts exist for every 3k photo), which guarantees the photo contradicts the negative and closes the spatial/numeracy vocabulary gap; LLM-written negatives are only useful with a VLM check against the photo (one-off, ~1 GPU-h).

findings.title: Measure the ceiling first: VQAScore of positive vs negative generations tells you whether the images differ at all, and by family
findings.detail: Raw DINO orders pos>neg at only 0.57-0.63 held-out. Two explanations: DINO cannot see the difference, or the 4-step w=1 student ignores the edited word so the images are the same. Scoring each held-out generation with VQAScore against the positive caption (and the negative against its own prompt) separates them: if VQAScore(neg-gen | c+) ~ VQAScore(pos-gen | c+) for a family, no anchor-based ranking can carry signal for that family and it should be dropped from training. Base-model within-caption rgb range is 0.13 vs 0.085 for the students, i.e. the distilled students already make the prompts' generations MORE similar to each other.
findings.evidence: probe JSONs: within-caption rgb range mean 0.1316 (base) vs 0.0854/0.0866 (naive/ours); per-family rgb (ours): colour 0.59, count 0.57, shape 0.61, spatial 0.63, 3d 0.63, verb 0.70, texture 0.74.
findings.consequence: Without the ceiling, a null head result cannot be attributed to the representation vs the generator, and the O1 escalation path in the design note cannot be triggered rationally.
findings.fix: P0, ~10 min on 1 GPU for 1,200 generations (t2v_metrics is vendored): add VQAScore columns to probe_heldout.py records; report per family the fraction of pairs where the negative's image actually contradicts c+ (VQAScore drop > 0.1). Use that fraction to weight or filter families in the next negatives file.

findings.title: Controls that separate 'evaluator moved' from 'student improved': frozen head, shuffled-label head, and a bigger probe; kappa->inf is redundant with ours
findings.detail: kappa -> infinity or lambda_rank = 0 with an identity head is bit-for-bit 'ours' (the no-grad rollouts do not touch the student or the RNG), so it needs no run. The informative nulls are: (i) B1 with the head trained on PERMUTED positives (the positive designated at random among the m prompts): same moving-reward dynamics and F3 gradient inflation, zero compositional information; if it matches B1, B1's effect is the artifact; (ii) B1 with a head trained offline (F1c) then FROZEN (or frozen after 500 updates): a stationary shaped reward whose lambda can be calibrated once; (iii) the A student probed with the identity head: if A's rollouts rank held-out pos>neg in RAW DINO above ours' 0.627, the student itself became prompt-discriminative regardless of the head. The probe at n=300 has SE ~0.02 (paired ours-naive rgb +0.023 +- 0.020, t=1.2), too coarse for the +-0.02 differences at stake.
findings.evidence: train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1379-1443 (rollouts never enter the student's graph in head mode); probe paired delta computed from probe/hp1_{naive,ours}_s0.json records.
findings.consequence: Without (i)-(iii) a positive B1/A result cannot be attributed, and without a larger probe the representation claim cannot be resolved.
findings.fix: Priority order and cost on 4xH100: probe n=1,000-1,500 with trained heads and the A student, 40 min on 1 GPU (P0); shuffled-label B1, 13 GPU-h/seed (P1, run only if B1 or A beats ours by > 0.01 at 3 seeds); frozen-head B1, 13 GPU-h/seed (P1, the cleanest version of the idea); argmin A, 27 GPU-h/seed (P2).

findings.title: Train the head on true DINO features (decode is cheap) or on features that retain colour and layout; DINO's invariances cap colour and left/right at chance
findings.detail: DINOv2 is trained with colour jitter, random grayscale (p=0.2) and horizontal flips, and the scorer mean-pools patches, so colour, mirror and layout information is largely removed before any head sees it; a head cannot recover it. This matches the probe (colour 0.49-0.59, count 0.57, spatial 0.58-0.63) and the repo's earlier within-prompt result for DINO. Training the head on P makes it worse still (P at chance). The repo already established that VAE decode costs ~61 ms and that the exact decode+DINO reward beats the projector reward at 3k and 118k.
findings.evidence: probe per-family rgb/latent tables; memory notes 'decode is cheap' and 'exact reward beats argmax'; OnlineScorer patch-mean (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:103-107).
findings.consequence: For the two CompBench categories that matter most to the paper (colour, spatial), the design has a structural ceiling independent of the ranking loss.
findings.fix: P1: in the offline head study (F1c) compare heads on (a) P(z_K), (b) DINO patch-mean of decoded z_K, (c) DINO patch tokens with a small attention head (keeps layout/count), (d) SigLIP/CLIP image embeddings as the anchor space (colour-sensitive by construction). If only (c)/(d) show held-out signal, the honest framing is that prompt-awareness comes from the feature choice, not from bending DINO. For a training arm, pair the head with --reward_mode rgb (exact decode+DINO reward, ~1.3x cost) so the head and the reward live in the same space; cost ~17 GPU-h/seed for a B1-style run.

findings.title: Probe captions overlap the projector's pretraining split and the probe requires >=2 negatives
findings.detail: 61 of the 300 probe captions are in P's train split and 9 in its val split (manifest.jsonl); the exclusion covers only the 3k pool. This does not leak into the head (trained on the 3k test split only) and is paired across models, but the 'P at chance held-out' statement is slightly optimistic for P (it is at chance even partly in-sample, which strengthens F1). The --min_negs 2 filter biases the probe toward captions with more editable spans than training (>=1).
findings.evidence: phaseW/latent_scorer/manifest.jsonl split field; probe_heldout.py:75-86.
findings.consequence: Absolute P numbers are not strictly held-out; comparisons between models remain valid.
findings.fix: Add the projector's train/val idx to the exclusion set (one line) and report the probe with min_negs 1 as well.

findings.title: In-training true-DINO monitors are too small to be informative, and rank/* metrics are rank-0's shard only
findings.detail: The RGB monitor decodes the last 8 buffered captions (acc_rgb swings 0.29-0.96) and the reward hacking monitor uses 32 predictions; rank_stats accumulate per rank but only rank 0's are logged (1/4 of the data). Decode is ~61 ms/image, so 64 captions x 4 prompts every 200 updates costs ~20 s.
findings.evidence: train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1437-1440 (rank_buf capped at 16), 1471 (rank_buf[-8:]), 1478 (is_main logging of local rank_stats).
findings.consequence: The one fixed evaluator available during training (true DINO) cannot be read, so 'student improved' cannot be tracked in-run.
findings.fix: Raise rank_buf to 64 and monitor all of it every 200 updates; all-reduce the rank_stats sums before logging.

verdicts.reason: Every cited fact reproduces. (1) Hook placement: phaseW/rank/rank_utils.py:70-79 sets `last = k == n-1`, enables grad only when `grad or (grad_last and last)`, and calls `hook.arm()` only on that last forward; the trainer passes `grad_last=(align is not None), hook=align` (train_pilot_frozen_s4j.py:1393-1394). There is no flag to arm it elsewhere (only --align_lambda/--align_layer/--align_lr exist, lines 571-573). (2) Sigmas: loading the SD3.5-medium FlowMatchEuler scheduler from the run's HF cache (shift 3.0) with set_timesteps(4) gives sigmas [1.0, 0.8577, 0.6022, 0.0089, 0.0], timesteps [1000, 857.69, 602.15, 8.93]; the run log logs/lsf-sd-W-train118k-151399.out line 9 prints the same `rollout sigmas [1.0, 0.858, 0.602, 0.009, 0.0]`. So the hooked forward's input is z_3 at sigma=0.0089 (timestep 8.93), and the last Euler step is z_K = z_3 + (0-0.0089)*v (rank_utils.py:80), i.e. delta-sigma = -0.00893. (3) Target: line 1421 `_tgt = head_apply(rank_head, _e.detach(), False).detach()` with `_e = proj(_zK)` (line 1396), so the target is a fixed (P frozen w.r.t. this loss, g detached) function of z_K ≈ z_3 — essentially the same tensor the hooked block just consumed. (4) Consistency branch never visits that noise level: `[window] score_idxs=[4,5,6,7] Kw=4` (log line 5), `stu_idx = [kt - deltas[kt]]` with delta in [1,3] (lines 1072-1073, args delta_min=1/delta_max=3), so student inputs are K=8 indices 1..6 = sigmas [0.9475, 0.8828, 0.8008, 0.6938, 0.548, 0.338]; index 7 (0.0089) is never reached, and lambda_real=0, reward states are picked from those same inputs.
